544277|2026-03.headline: Waaree FY26 revenue rose ~84% to INR26,537 crore and operating EBITDA 117% to INR5,909 crore, but Q4 margin fell to ~18.6% on commodity, freight and mix pressures.
544277|2026-03.overview: FY26 was a record year: revenue from operations of INR26,537 crore (+84% YoY), operating EBITDA of INR5,909 crore (22.27% margin vs 18.84%) and PAT of INR3,884 crore (+101%). Q4 revenue was INR8,480 crore (+111% YoY) and operating EBITDA INR1,576 crore, with margin down sharply from the prior quarter as silver and copper costs, freight spikes, lower overseas mix and in-house DCR cell shortfall weighed. Management guided FY27 operating EBITDA to INR7,000-7,700 crore and framed the Waaree 2.0 capex (~$3.5 billion) as the driver, with most cell and module capex completing in FY27 and benefits from H2 FY27 onward. Operating cash conversion fell to about 27% as export shipments were stuck on logistics delays and inventory built up.

segments.name: Module manufacturing
segments.commentary: FY26 production 12.6 GW (+77%), sales about 12 GW; Q4 production 4.2 GW (+104% YoY) and Q4 sales 4.1 GW. Capacity ~26 GW, described as the largest non-Chinese module maker.

segments.name: Cell manufacturing
segments.commentary: Operational cell capacity 5.4 GW (largest in India); Q4 cell production 0.7 GW. A 10 GW cell facility is due in H2 FY27, taking cell capacity to ~15.4 GW.

segments.name: Revenue mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: Utility/IPP/C&I 34.7%, overseas 33%, retail 20.8%, EPC 11.6%. Retail revenue INR5,515 crore (+84%). Q4 overseas share fell to ~21% from ~32% in Q3.

segments.name: US manufacturing
segments.commentary: 1.6 GW plant ramped; 2.6 GW more to go live within six months, taking US capacity to 4.2 GW. IRA benefit ~$0.07/Wp, ~$40 million in FY26, to rise with new capacity.

segments.name: Order book
segments.commentary: ~INR53,000 crore excluding retail (~20% of revenue), up from ~INR47,000 crore a year ago but down ~INR7,000 crore QoQ per analyst. ~65-70% is overseas, to be delivered over 3-4 years. More than INR8,400 crore delivered already.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guided at INR7,000-7,700 crore (about 20-25% growth on FY26 INR5,909 crore).
Management says the margin benefit from in-house DCR cells starts in H2 FY27 when the 10 GW cell line goes live; H1 is a transition.
Long-range planning assumption: 19-20% EBITDA margin sustained for a decade.
Cell utilisation assumed 80-85% for FY28 on 15.4 GW capacity; 28 GW modules, 4 GW inverters, 20,000 MVA transformers and 1 GW electrolyser to run at full throttle in FY28.
Capex of ~$3.5 billion (INR30,000 crore) over the next two years; core module and cell capex complete in FY27, ingot wafer and part of battery in FY28; full Waaree 2.0 benefits seen in FY29.
Cell line transition from M10R to G12R expected to lift output and realisation by 10-12% within about a quarter; module output back to ~330 MW a month within two months.
Investor Day to be held; enabling board resolution for fundraise of up to ~INR10,000 crore approved, with shareholder approval to follow.
capex_capacity: Battery (BESS): 20 GWh planned, phase 1 of 3.5 GWh in FY27 (Gujarat), phase 2 of 16.5 GWh in FY28; capex ~INR10,000 crore.
Ingot wafer: 10 GW at Nagpur, capex ~INR6,200 crore (up from INR5,100 crore earlier with 6 GW to 10 GW); completion FY28.
PV glass: 2,500 TPD approved at ~INR3,900 crore capex, production expected within 24 months; supports ~16-17 GW of modules.
Inverters: 4 GW at Sarodhi, Gujarat (~INR180 crore); 3 GW commissioned, remaining 1 GW in FY27.
Transformers: current ~4,000 MVA; adding 16,000 MVA to reach 20,000 MVA at Alwar (~INR192 crore) in FY27.
Hydrogen: 1 GW electrolyser at Dungri, Gujarat (~INR676 crore capex); electrolyser PLI INR444 crore and hydrogen PLI ~INR510 crore.
Acquired ~55% of Associated Power Structures Ltd (APSL) for ~INR1,225 crore for T&D entry; Oman polysilicon stake acquired for non-Chinese supply.
Module lines: 3 lines converted to G12R (ramping), 3 lines remain Mono PERC, 5 lines still on M10R TOPCon, to convert over about one quarter.
demand_pricing: Domestic DCR module pricing INR21-22/Wp; non-DCR utility INR15-16/Wp, with retail carrying a premium; commodity increases are being passed through to new orders.
Silver and copper cost increases, freight spikes and a lower overseas share weighed on Q4 margin; management said customers are now accepting the higher commodity-linked prices.
ALMM-II (domestic cell mandate) takes effect June 2026; C&I and mid-market decisions were deferred pending clarity, which slowed local offtake.
India installed 44.6 GW of solar in FY26; module consumption was about 50-55 GW. Management sees DCR-compliant cell capacity at ~30 GW for ALMM-II.
US FEOC rules from April 2026 require non-Chinese cells and components, which management says is driving new US orders.
BESS pricing around $110-120/MWh cited for India and US; BESS margin guided at 18-20% before policy support.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating EBITDA margin fall sharply QoQ, and what are the DCR and non-DCR realisations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited silver and copper cost spikes, freight cost surge, a lower overseas mix and DCR cell shortfall. DCR modules INR21-22/Wp; utility non-DCR INR15-16/Wp, with a retail premium.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the export mix low in Q4 and what is the order book composition?
qa_highlights.answer: Export shipments were stuck on Middle East logistics delays, so inventory rose. About 65-70% of the INR53,000 crore order book is overseas, delivered over 3-4 years; retail (~20% of revenue) is excluded.

qa_highlights.question: How will the FY27 EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore be achieved, and what drives margin?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 is a transition from 5.4 GW to 15.4 GW of cells; the 10 GW cell line in H2 lifts in-house DCR supply. Pre-startup costs for new projects are included in guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the ingot-wafer capex rise and its timeline move to FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity was raised from 6 GW to 10 GW and sites moved from Odisha to Gujarat and Nagpur, causing the delay. The new figure covers the full 10 GW.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cash conversion cycle and working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory built up because overseas shipments were delayed. Customer advances stayed steady but production nearly doubled, diluting working capital days. Management expects cash conversion of 70-100% at normalised inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What are the BESS unit economics and FY29 revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: BESS margin guided at 18-20% without policy support. Management declined to give FY29 revenue guidance, pointing to the 20 GWh capacity and $110-120/MWh pricing.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on the 10 GW cell line commissioning in H2 FY27 and on the G12R ramp; Q4 showed sharp margin compression.
Working capital and cash conversion (~27%) need to normalise as stuck export inventory ships.
ALMM-II timing uncertainty is deferring C&I and mid-market orders; order book fell ~INR7,000 crore QoQ.
Commodity (silver, copper) and freight volatility; pricing pass-through to new orders is unproven.
Execution risk on ~$3.5 billion capex across BESS, glass, ingot-wafer and US plants, plus fundraise of up to INR10,000 crore.
Overcapacity concerns in the module sector; management argues demand and supply balance once ALMM-II/III take effect.
544277|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the long-term Waaree 2.0 story and on FY26 results. Noticeably defensive and detailed when explaining the Q4 margin drop, cash conversion and order-book sequential decline, often attributing them to temporary logistics and transition factors. Several answers on BESS economics, the fundraise, Indosolar and ALMM-II timing were deferred or left unquantified.

financial_highlights.change: Above prior guidance of INR5,500-6,000 crore
+70% YoY; margin fell sharply QoQ (analyst cited ~590 bps decline)
vs INR644 crore in Q4 FY25
Down from over 100% in prior period per analyst; management says 70-100% normalised

key_quotes: Our capital allocation follows a simple principle, book and build, which means every rupee we deploy is backed by confirmed demand and a clear path to returns.
The safest assumption there will be is your 19 %-20% margin consistent for a decade long at least.
So, we really don't foresee any scenario anytime next 5, 10 years of time will be the supply is going to be much higher than demand.
So, if you keep the inventory at normalized levels, the same number will go back to the normalized level of 70% to 100% conversion of cash from current 27%.

544277|2026-06.headline: Waaree Q1 FY27 revenue rose 79.2% YoY to INR7,932 crore and order book hit a record INR61,500 crore, though operating EBITDA margin was 18.2%.
544277|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 79.2% YoY to about INR7,932 crore, with operating EBITDA up 44.4% to about INR1,440 crore at an 18.2% margin and PAT of INR892 crore (11% margin, up 15.4%). Management attributed margin pressure to higher global raw material costs, softer US exports from delayed clearances, and inventory built ahead of second-half-weighted dispatches. Order book rose to INR61,500 crore after INR16,000 crore of net inflows against about INR7,300 crore executed. Management reaffirmed FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore, pinning the margin recovery on rising captive cell integration and US local manufacturing.

segments.name: Revenue mix
segments.commentary: Utility IPP and C&I 39.7%, retail 30.2%, overseas 21.2%, EPC and O&M 8.9% of Q1 FY27 revenue. Utility/IPP/C&I share was 52.1% in FY25.

segments.name: Retail (B2C)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR2,289 crore, up 130% YoY; management guides INR9,000-10,000 crore for FY27.

segments.name: Overseas / US
segments.commentary: US domestic revenue INR1,322 crore and direct exports INR287 crore. US plant produced about 230 MW in Q1, earning roughly USD12-13 million of IRA incentives.

segments.name: Cell manufacturing (India)
segments.commentary: 5.4 GW capacity at 62% utilisation; about 800 MW of DCR cell made in Q1. Integrated cell lines show 35-40% margin per management.

segments.name: Modules (India and US)
segments.commentary: India module capacity 24.2 GW at about 50% annualised utilisation; US module capacity 1.6 GW at about 59%. Management expects US utilisation of 75-80% in coming quarters.

segments.name: BESS / storage
segments.commentary: Automated BESS container capacity of 5.15 GWh started, versus 3.5 GWh originally planned. A 1,520 MWh BESS EPC order was won.

segments.name: Transmission and transformers
segments.commentary: Waaree Transpower began commercial production of a 17.6 MVA inverter-duty transformer. WRTL acquired about 55% of Associated Power Structures for about INR1,225 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 operating EBITDA guidance of INR7,000-7,700 crore reaffirmed.
FY28 ballpark of about INR7,000 crore EBITDA mentioned by Varun Goenka; FY28 expected to see about 16-18 GW module and about 10 GW cell production.
Cell-to-module integration ratio to rise from about 20% to about 65% within 2-3 quarters.
Cell production to rise from about 800 MW in Q1 to about 1.2 GW in Q2 and about 1.5 GW in Q3.
Module utilisation to reach 70-75% in Q3 and Q4; management expects 80-85% over 2-3 quarters as integration rises.
US IRA incentive receipts expected quarterly from Q3-Q4 FY27 via refund or sale of credits; US production of 400-500 MW per quarter from Q3.
Management aspires to a near INR1 lakh crore revenue vision in less than 4-5 years.
capex_capacity: Announced capex programme about INR31,500 crore; about INR9,450 crore deployed as of 30 June. Phasing is about 30% in FY27, 40% in FY28 and 30% in FY29.

FY27 additions: 2.6 GW US modules, 10 GW Indian cell (Gujarat, ALMM-II applied, equipment on site, commercial start expected from about Q3), 100 KTPA T&D EPC, 20 GVA transformers, 4 GW inverters, 1 GW electrolysers.
FY28: 10 GW ingot and wafer at Nagpur, construction started. FY29: 2,500 TPD solar glass (about INR3,900 crore, greenfield approved) and 16.5 GWh BESS plant.
Indian cell capacity to reach 15.4 GW against 24.2 GW module capacity by FY27-end; US BESS cell 3.5 GWh to commission within FY27, with 95% site construction done.
Potential QIP of about INR10,000 crore approved by Board and shareholders; timing depends on market conditions.
demand_pricing: Order book INR61,500 crore as of 28 July 2026 (25.2 GW), up from about INR53,000 crore at FY26-end; geographic mix India about 40%, US about 36%, exports about 24%.
Realisations per watt: exports USD0.25-0.26; DCR USD0.20-0.25; non-DCR USD0.13-0.14. Order book realisations seen at USD0.24-0.25 for near quarters; long-range DCR orders at USD0.21-0.22.
Non-DCR offtake delayed by developers in Q1; ALMM-II effective 1 June with about a 5-6 month window, leading to expected offtake from Q2.
Top 5 customers 27.1% of sales (from 33% in FY26); top 10 at 37.1% (from 47%).
Imported cell about USD0.04-0.045/W versus Indian manufacturing cost of USD0.07-0.08/W; DCR market price about USD0.12-0.13/W.
US market had about six months of installation lull due to tariff uncertainty; management reports recent order and enquiry pickup, including data-centre demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expansion timeline for 10 GW cell and wafer and battery capacity over FY28-FY29?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 28 GW modules, 15.4 GW cells, 4 GW inverters and 20 GVA transformers by FY27-end; FY28 to see about 16-18 GW modules and about 10 GW cell output. The 10 GW Indian cell facility adds from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Why did module gross margin fall, and what are the recovery levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Lower IRA realisation in Q1 because US dispatches came from OEM manufacturing; delayed non-DCR offtake; softer exports. Levers are DCR cell output, US local scaling, exports from August, and non-DCR offtake over the six-month window.

qa_highlights.question: How are US export and US local manufacturing margins structured?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports from India earn about USD0.04-0.05/W EBITDA. US local manufacturing nets about USD0.055-0.06/W after expenses, with IRA incentive of USD0.07/W. Management guides total US local realisation and EBITDA at USD0.07-0.08/W, helped by a USD0.01-0.02/W cut in US conversion cost.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a lower-cost import option for cells compared with domestic manufacturing?
qa_highlights.answer: Imported cell is about USD0.04-0.045/W against Indian manufacturing cost of USD0.07-0.08/W and DCR market price of USD0.12-0.13/W.

qa_highlights.question: What is the BESS volume and earnings outlook for FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: The 5.15 GWh container line is live and order book is building. The 3.5 GWh BESS cell line is due to start commercially in FY27. FEOC-compliant cell realisations are about 25-30% above Chinese pricing, with non-FEOC at USD75-80/kWh versus Chinese USD50-55/kWh.

qa_highlights.question: What is the QIP plan and funding need?
qa_highlights.answer: Board and shareholders approved about INR10,000 crore of fundraising including equity. Management says FY27 EBITDA is broadly sufficient to fund the capex and it will wait for the right market window. Balance capex is about INR22,000 crore over three years.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from raw material inflation and a lower IRA realisation mix in Q1; watch whether 18.2% operating EBITDA margin recovers toward the FY27 guidance band.
Second-half weighted order book and inventory build; utilisation of India modules around 50% annualised in Q1 versus a 70-75% target for Q3-Q4.
Timing of the 10 GW Indian cell commissioning (targeted by December) and ALMM-II extension window; the non-DCR offtake ramp is unconfirmed.
US export clearance delays and the start of US local line output from August; US IRA incentive monetisation timing.
Capex execution across INR31,500 crore programme and the glass capex decision, with an update promised in about one quarter.
Pending QIP and funding plan; BESS Make-in-India incentive is not yet announced.
544277|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on long-term demand, order book and capacity milestones, but candid about Q1 margin and dispatch shortfalls. Management repeatedly tied recovery to specific dated levers and reaffirmed guidance. Responses on glass capex, BESS incentives and QIP timing were less specific.
key_quotes: Our order book stands at approximately INR61,500 crores, the highest in our history, up from INR50,000 crores just a quarter ago, with about INR16,000 crores in new orders won in this quarter alone.
Our cell-to-module integration ratio is going to rise from roughly around 20% currently to around 65% in next two to three quarters, close to a threefold increase.
It is on this trend that we affirm and reaffirm our 2027 operating EBITDA guidance, what we have stated in our last call.

financial_highlights.change: US domestic INR1,322 crore; direct export INR287 crore
net cash balance sheet as of 30 June

544279|2026-03.headline: Godavari Biorefineries FY26 total income rose 6% to INR2,000 crore and EBITDA 15.8% to INR139 crore, with Q4 EBITDA of INR92 crore (16.2% margin).
544279|2026-03.overview: FY26 total income was INR2,000.2 crore (up 6% from INR1,886.9 crore) and EBITDA was INR139.3 crore (up 15.8% from INR120.3 crore), with full-year margin around 7%. Profit after tax was INR3.5 crore versus a loss in FY25. Q4 revenue from operations was INR564 crore, EBITDA INR92 crore (margin 16.2% versus 9.8% in Q3), and PAT INR52.9 crore versus INR8.3 crore in Q3, driven by a record 2.5 million tonne crushing season. Management said the bio-based chemicals outlook is stronger from Q1 FY27, helped by higher import costs and narrowing fossil-to-bio price gaps, while the 200 KLPD grain distillery is nearing commissioning trials.

financial_highlights.change: stabilised; pressure in parts of the year from feedstock cost, improvement in H2
sequential recovery; QoQ comparison not stated
more than doubled QoQ from margin of 9.8% in Q3
up from INR8.3 crore in Q3 FY26
down about 32% YoY, after INR240 crore debt repayment in FY25

segments.name: Integrated sugar, ethanol and co-generation
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue about INR1,383 crore and EBITDA INR97.4 crore (up 19% YoY). Q4 revenue about INR411 crore, with margin gains from higher crushing volumes and better recoveries; highest-ever cane crushing of 2.5 million tonnes.

segments.name: Bio-based chemicals
segments.commentary: FY26 segment revenue INR578 crore; Q4 revenue about INR147 crore. Specialty chemicals rose to 61% of segment revenue from 58% YoY, though geopolitical disruption hit sales and the call did not give segment EBITDA.

segments.name: Ethanol
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR658 crore on improved B-heavy molasses availability; about 98 million litres sold (ethanol blending programme, ENA and other grades). About 81% of volume went to EBP per analyst question, which management did not dispute.

segments.name: Jivana (consumer business)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR129 crore; management cites growing retail presence across South India, with no margin or growth rate disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Management expects stronger bio-based chemicals performance from Q1 FY27, with debottlenecking benefits from FY25 showing through in FY27.

200 KLPD grain-based distillery (about 60 million litres a year) to start commissioning trials in June 2026, with some business in Q2 FY27; larger benefits expected from the ethanol year starting November.
Government ethanol pricing and EBP targets expected around September or October 2026; management will then give clearer economics for the new capacity.
Management said the company may use surplus ethanol for its own ethyl acetate and chemicals production, given higher imported ethanol costs.
DME (CO2 and hydrogen) pilot plant research expected to take another 3 to 6 months before a clearer view.
capex_capacity: 200 KLPD grain-based distillery: most equipment on site per management, with one or two items awaited; commissioning trials targeted for June 2026 (management earlier said Q1 FY27 and next month).
Adds approximately 60 million litres of annual ethanol capacity; management did not give capex, asset turns or EBITDA potential at normalised utilisation.
Maize-based ethanol to be bought under the government maize price for the blending programme; multi-feedstock benefits expected once the maize facility is running.
Bagasse supplies about 85% of energy and coal about 15%; energy costs described as stable.
Sathgen Therapeutics step-down subsidiary formed; CDSCO application for preliminary efficacy trial of the triple-negative breast cancer molecule planned for next quarter.
demand_pricing: Management reports higher import costs and narrower fossil-to-bio price gap, leading to an expected uptick in bio-based chemical demand in FY27. More than 20 bio-based molecules are made; some faced raw material and freight disruption from the West Asia crisis.
Ethanol prices are set by the government: management quoted net realisation of about INR60-plus/litre for B-heavy molasses, INR65-plus for juice and about INR72 for maize.
Ethanol supply is in surplus under the blending programme; industry has asked the government to revise ethanol prices, and management said a decision lies with the government.
Draft standards for E85, E100 and beyond E20 are cited as future demand drivers, but management gave no timeline for flex-fuel policy.
Management said the company is still weighing ethyl acetate margins against its long-term specialty chemicals goal, and that ethyl acetate was run when margins were better.

qa_highlights.question: Why did profitability fall from INR95 crore (31 March 2025) to INR66 crore (31 March 2026), and what will profitability look like next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed margin pressure to a higher sugarcane price for the last season without a matching increase in sugar MSP or ethanol prices. It pointed to better bio-based chemicals and maize ethanol contributions in the coming year, without a figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net realisation on ethanol by feedstock?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said net realisation is about INR60-plus per litre from B-heavy molasses, INR65-plus from juice and about INR72 from maize; all prices are government-declared.

qa_highlights.question: Has the grain distillery equipment arrived and what margins are underwritten for maize ethanol?
qa_highlights.answer: Almost all equipment is on site with one or two items pending, and commissioning trials are targeted for next month. Larger benefits are expected from the November ethanol year; management did not give a spread figure.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the specialty mix fall, and was the ethyl acetate ramp deliberate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was partly a margin call, since ethanol supply is in surplus and ethyl acetate margins were attractive, while the long-term aim is still more specialty chemicals.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DME pilot status and what milestones are needed before commercialisation?
qa_highlights.answer: The lab work at ICT is complete and the pilot plant is running; management expects 3 to 6 more months of research before it can give a better answer.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a change in the ethanol price or policy outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Price revisions are for the government to decide. The industry has asked for higher blend pricing given sugarcane price rises over three years, and management pointed to E85/E100 draft standards as future demand support.

risks_watch: Ethanol prices are government-set, and the industry is seeking a revision; no timeline was given. Sugar MSP and ethanol prices were unchanged despite a higher cane price, which squeezed margins.
The 200 KLPD grain distillery is still in commissioning trials; utilisation, capex and maize spreads are not yet disclosed, so near-term contribution is uncertain.
West Asia-linked disruption affected raw material supply and freight for some bio-based chemicals in Q4; management said logistics hit the chemicals segment.
Specialty chemical share rose to 61%, but bio-based revenue was flat in FY26 (INR578 crore) and the revenue mix was largely unchanged from FY25.
Monsoon and cane pricing for next season remain open questions, and the DME and TNBC programmes are early-stage, with a 2 to 3 year timeline for out-licensing.
544279|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on the bio-based and ethanol outlook, but cautious and non-committal on pricing and policy. Management gave no numbers for the grain distillery's economics or for the TNBC and DME timelines, and deferred several questions to later periods or the government.
key_quotes: So, we are definitely seeing a stronger outlook in this financial year and this will be apparent from in the -- from this quarter onwards, that's the first point.
We achieved it as a nation by five years in advance.

The margin pressure took place because the government had announced a increased price of sugarcane for the last crushing season and did not increase the MSP of sugar and neither did they increase the price of the ethanol blend.

544279|2026-06.headline: Godavari Biorefineries Q1 FY27 EBITDA fell to INR2.6 crores (0.5% margin) as sugar-ethanol losses offset a 53% jump in bio-based chemicals EBITDA.
544279|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations rose 4.6% YoY to INR557.9 crores and total income rose 4.9% to INR559.9 crores, but EBITDA dropped to INR2.6 crores from INR6.5 crores. Bio-based chemicals grew revenue 19.4% to INR168.7 crores with EBITDA up 53% to INR19.2 crores, while the integrated sugar, cogeneration and ethanol segment's EBITDA loss widened to INR14.6 crores. The company commissioned a 200 KLPD grain-based distillery at Sameerwadi, taking total distillery capacity to 800 KLPD, and announced a further INR25 crores debottlenecking investment in bio-based specialty chemicals. Consolidated net loss widened to INR19.3 crores from INR16 crores.

segments.name: Bio-based chemicals
segments.commentary: Revenue INR168.7 crores (+19.4% YoY) and EBITDA INR19.2 crores (+53%), margin 11.4% vs 8.9%, attributed to product mix and debottlenecking benefits. Management guides to about INR190 crores revenue next quarter.

segments.name: Integrated sugar, cogeneration and ethanol
segments.commentary: Revenue INR377.9 crores, flat YoY, with EBITDA loss of INR14.6 crores vs INR4.5 crores loss a year ago. Management cited feedstock conditions, higher manufacturing cost and ethanol tender allotments; better sugar realisations provided partial support.

guidance_outlook: Bio-based chemicals revenue expected at about INR190 crores in Q2 FY27, sustained thereafter.
INR25 crores debottlenecking in bio-based specialty chemicals, expected to complete by early FY28, targeting about INR240 crores quarterly revenue at full penetration.
Evaluating 160 KLPD fungible capacity addition within the existing 800 KLPD, mainly a maize grain-preparation front end; no firm timeline or return numbers given.
Debt levels expected broadly similar, with no major change in debt-equity structure.
DME pilot trial results expected by March 2027.

Triple-negative breast cancer molecule: CDSCO permission for preliminary efficacy trials hoped for by end of Q3 FY27; about INR20 crores spend over the next 2 to 3 years to reach preliminary efficacy.
capex_capacity: Commissioned 200 KLPD grain-based distillery at Sameerwadi in Q1 FY27; total distillery capacity now 800 KLPD.
Additional INR25 crores investment in debottlenecking bio-based specialty chemicals, completion expected early FY28.
Evaluating a 160 KLPD maize grain-preparation front end to use idle fermentation and distillation capacity if sugar diversion rises.
Bio-butanol: MoU with Synthomer for use as chemical intermediate; engaging on a government call for butanol pathways.
DME in pilot trials, progressing as planned.
demand_pricing: Management sees rising customer interest in bio-based specialty chemicals in India and overseas, driven by supply-chain reliability and a narrower fossil-to-green price gap.

Grain/maize ethanol featured prominently in the current ethanol tender, per management.
Closing sugar inventory about 65,000 tonnes; management estimated 15,000 to 20,000 tonnes under long-term contracts, not confirmed.

qa_highlights.question: Commercialisation timeline for DME and bio-butanol?
qa_highlights.answer: DME pilot results expected by March 2027, with commercial discussion only after success. Bio-butanol has a Synthomer MoU as chemical intermediate, and the company is engaging on a government butanol initiative.

qa_highlights.question: Next milestones and out-licensing for the TNBC molecule?
qa_highlights.answer: CDSCO application filed; next milestone is permission for preliminary efficacy trials, hoped by end of Q3 FY27. Company plans to out-license after efficacy data.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainability of chemical margins and steady-state potential?

544285|2026-06.headline: Swiggy guides Quick Commerce contribution margin to 0 to -100 bps for growth, with 4-week cumulative NOV growth at 10% vs 1% prior.

Take-rate gains were attributed to brand monetisation, advertising and user-fee changes, with management calling them sustainable. Food delivery growth was about 18% adjusted for cancellations, with 18-20% YoY guidance maintained, and management dismissed zero-commission competition from Toing's rivals as unsustainable. Retail market share rose to 10.1% for the full year and 10.4% in Q4. Management set a long-term IFRS combined ratio target of about 99% by FY29, which it says translates to a mid-to-high teens ROE. Commission regulation remains an open question pending regulator guidance.

544294|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 62% YoY to about INR142 crores; FY26 revenue up 87% to INR485 crores, but margins fell and management guided to similar growth in FY27.

Margins were lower than previously guided, which management attributed to qualification and investment costs for new semiconductor and space customers. Management guided to similar growth in FY27 and said margins would improve, and it is pursuing a QIP sized at about 7-10% of market cap.

544296|2026-03.headline: Nisus standalone core revenue rose 110% YoY to INR 141 crore and PAT to INR 68 crore (48% margin) in FY26, with Q4 PAT of INR 11 crore.

Working capital dependence (INR 261 crore) and finance cost reduction; IPO proceeds still being drawn down.

qa_highlights.question: Merchant roll-out: what numbers and how should it be modelled?

544307|2026-03.headline: Vishal Mega Mart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 22.2% to INR 3,114 crore with same-store sales growth of 13.2%, while management flagged input inflation from May.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 SSSG acceleration, and was there pre-buying?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a general consumption uptick after income tax and GST cuts, plus higher growth investment in the quarter. It did not frame it as pre-buying.

qa_highlights.question: How will private-label pricing respond to rising leader-brand prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Management committed to keep the discount to leader brands at least at 40% for apparel, and to try to widen it if possible.

qa_highlights.question: How did the company handle the cotton inflation of 2021-22?

qa_highlights.question: Are price increases neutral, incremental or negative to apparel sales?

segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 1,133 crore (+31%), EBITDA INR 398 crore (+42%), margin 35% vs 32%; occupancy 63% (+5 pp), TRevPAR ~INR 60,000. Same-store revenue +15%, EBITDA +29%. Q4 revenue +18% to INR 421 crore, EBITDA +19% to INR 198 crore, occupancy 75%, TRevPAR INR 90,818 (+18%).

segments.name: Annuity
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 127 crore (+2%), EBITDA INR 113 crore (+2%), margin 89%. FY26 revenue INR 505 crore (+4%), EBITDA INR 452 crore (+3%).

guidance_outlook: Management said the company does not give formal revenue or earnings guidance; medium-term aspiration is low-teen revenue growth and high-teen EBITDA growth once conditions normalise.
Visibility is limited to Q1 FY27; management expects the quarter not to be derailed, citing displaced March demand, group and MICE bookings, and a low Q1 FY26 base from Operation Sindoor.
India occupancy targeted at 75% in the medium term (Pune); Conrad and Anantara in Maldives targeted above 65% occupancy in the medium term.
Capex of around INR 1,000 crore over the next three years (Bangalore AC by Marriott, Sri Lanka Ritz-Carlton Reserve, FF&E), to be funded mainly by internal accruals.
Management said FY26 would have crossed INR 1,200 crore EBITDA without March 2026 geopolitical disruption, versus INR 992 crore in FY25 (about 20% growth).
capex_capacity: AC by Marriott conversion of Whitefield (Bangalore) is on plan, with completion by March 2027.
Varanasi Marriott is in construction and design; completion targeted in FY28.
Ritz-Carlton Reserve in Sri Lanka is in design and planning; completion in FY28, one of nine Ritz-Carlton Reserves globally.

Hilton Goa plans: rebrand and add 60-70 keys; Sol de Goa (21-key boutique resort) to be combined into the same portfolio, targeting about 200 keys together; Batim Land branded residence at design stage with capital raise planned.
Soho House Delhi expected to complete within about two years. Mundra opportunity put on hold; Narmada Estates (East Pune land parcel) identified for annuity development.
demand_pricing: India: Pune ADR for four Pune hotels averaged INR 15,152 in Q4 FY26, comparable to gateway cities; management said the company controls over 65% of the luxury market in Pune. Customer mix is about 60% foreign and 40% domestic.
Pune office absorption was about 7 million sq ft last year, with roughly 40 million sq ft estimated over the next five years; management said luxury-hotel demand is linked to office absorption.

Maldives: Q1 demand shifting toward China, Russia, Korea, Japan with shorter booking windows. Management said Maldives is connected to about 90 destinations through 40-45 direct flights. An industry data point cited by an analyst showed Male arrivals down about 25% YoY in April and about 15% in the first 10 days of May; management said it could not reconcile this data.
Maldives diesel: management said existing island stocks covered 1.5-2 months and that diesel repricing would have an impact, with timing and size uncertain.

Maldives F&B contribution to international revenue was 39% and rooms 49%; F&B grew about 39% YoY in the cited segment (management later said growth was about 10%), attributed partly to Raaya's all-inclusive allocation.

qa_highlights.question: How will FY27 unfold given March 2026 disruption, and how is Pune's outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 is visible only through Q1, with some volatility but no expected derailment; over time it sees low-teen revenue and high-teen EBITDA growth. Pune demand is driven by GCCs (about 20% of India's GCC market), IT, manufacturing, MICE and weddings.

qa_highlights.question: How much has business recovered in April-May, and how much of FY27 growth is base effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited displacement business from March, credit lines on group and MICE bookings, and a low Q1 FY26 base after Operation Sindoor. It said the company is moving northwards, with no quantified April or May figures given.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plans and cash flow use over three years?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,000 crore of capex over three years, mostly from internal accruals. FY26 cash generation was about INR 850 crore; INR 400 crore went to debt reduction, INR 200 crore to acquisitions (Hilton Goa, Soho House), and INR 200 crore to CWIP and advances. Management said headroom to the FY25 debt level of INR 2,300 crore is about INR 900 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did India Q4 EBITDA fall while revenue rose?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 FY25 included about INR 8 crore government grant and INR 1.5 crore electricity credit income, while Q4 FY26 had INR 5 crore prior-period electricity charge and INR 2.5 crore grant. Adjusted EBITDA was INR 96 crore (FY25) and INR 102 crore (FY26), about 6% growth.

qa_highlights.question: Maldives traffic data and diesel exposure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged cancellations and Middle East air disruption, but cited new flights from Russia, China, Australia and Malaysia. It said diesel repricing will have an impact, with timing uncertain. Luxury resorts historically saw little dip in volatile periods.

qa_highlights.question: Margin levers in India and Maldives, and any business-leisure mix shift?
qa_highlights.answer: India margin rose to 40% from 37% on ADR-led operating leverage. Maldives margin rose to 35% from 32% through occupancy, solar projects, cluster procurement and channel mix. Management saw no material change in India business or leisure mix.

risks_watch: Maldives arrivals and occupancy: conflicting YoY arrival data, Middle East air disruption, and diesel repricing on island operations.
India occupancy fell to about 64% for FY26 and 69% in Q4 (vs 71%); Aloft Whitefield rebranding shutdown and travel softness weighed on Q4.
Q4 EBITDA growth of 28% depends on FX gains of INR 74 crore; underlying growth was about 8%.
Q1 FY27 visibility is limited to one quarter given geopolitical and aviation volatility.
Execution on Varanasi (FY28), Ritz-Carlton Sri Lanka (FY28), Whitefield AC (March 2027) and Hilton Goa rebranding; Mundra on hold.
544321|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on FY26 results and portfolio strength, but cautious on near-term travel: management acknowledged March disruption and Maldives volatility, and gave no quantified April-May trends. It was defensive on the Maldives arrival data and the F&B/room revenue split questioned by analysts.
key_quotes: Ventive is no longer just a collection of high- quality assets. We are now operating a scaled hospitality platform with multiple growth engines, clear portfolio logic and increasing financial strength.
So all in all, we have around INR 500 crores cash today and even if I reach to INR 2,300crores debt, which was the debt as on FY25, I am sitting on INR 900 crores headroom for debt.
Maldives is connected to 90* different destinations through about 40 -45 direct flights.

544321|2026-06.headline: Consolidated revenue rose 7% to INR554 crores, but EBITDA fell about INR16 crores as Maldives diesel costs spiked; India grew 16% at INR74 crores.
544321|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 7% YoY to INR554 crores and consolidated EBITDA was INR205 crores at a 37% margin. The decline in EBITDA was attributed almost entirely to Maldives fuel and ancillary costs, which rose to INR38 crores from INR19 crores as diesel prices roughly doubled from pre-war levels in April-May. India delivered 13% revenue growth and 16% EBITDA growth, with occupancy and ADR both up. Reported PAT of INR124 crores was inflated by a INR102 crore deferred tax reversal following the tax regime switch.

Broadly flat; about 3% growth adjusted for one-off transaction costs

segments.commentary: Revenue INR218 crores (+5%) but EBITDA INR32 crores (-32%); fuel and ancillary costs rose to INR38 crores from INR19 crores. Excluding the fuel spike, management says EBITDA would have grown about 10%.

segments.name: Annuity (commercial/leased assets)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR128 crores (+3%) and EBITDA INR111 crores at 87% margin; committed occupancy 98%. Narmada Estates in Pune was recently added.

qa_highlights.question: What drove simultaneous occupancy and ADR gains in India in a seasonally soft quarter, and is there headroom in Pune?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to Pune dominance (about 65% of luxury inventory), MICE, corporate demand in IT/BFSI micro markets and weddings; it expects Pune occupancy to stabilise in the high 70s and sees 200-300 luxury and upper-upscale room nights a day added from office growth.

qa_highlights.question: Where do India margins settle, and is there operating leverage beyond cost savings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the solar capex (about INR60 crores, 3-year payback) could add roughly 4-5% to margin from Q1 next year, and that high occupancy is driving operating leverage.

qa_highlights.question: What is Maldives demand doing in April-June, July and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: India source-market demand rose to about 9% from 6%; China and Russia grew at double-digit occupancy; July tourist arrivals were back to 2025 levels with only 27 disrupted flights versus about 170 earlier.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Sahyadri/Kelzai acquisition be funded, and what is the threshold for acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said funding will mix debt and internal accruals, with tourism incentive subsidies of 15-20% of capital expected and operations in about 2 to 2.5 years; debt to be drawn in stages as needed. The acquisition criteria answer was not captured clearly in the transcript.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Maldives EBITDA decline was diesel versus operations, and what is the FY27 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline entirely to fuel: fuel bill up INR17 crores plus INR2 crores indirect, total about INR19 crores; ex-fuel Maldives EBITDA would have grown about 10%. Diesel was still about 20% below spot due to cluster procurement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Goa Hilton performance and expansion timing and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said occupancy and revenue are improving post-acquisition (104 keys), gave no unit-level numbers, and said the 50-plus key extension and refurbishment are in planning, with delivery around FY29-FY30; it expects to conservatively double EBITDA with the pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Why has Sri Lanka Arugam Bay commissioning moved from FY28 to around FY30?
qa_highlights.answer: Permissions are the constraint due to environmental sensitivity, about 1.5 km of shoreline and adjacency to Yala National Park; completions and formalities are near, with target around FY30.

qa_highlights.question: What are July and August trends for Maldives, and what do Q3/Q4 look like?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify August EBITDA margin, which depends on the war; it said occupancy remains strong and bookings on the books for Q3 and Q4 look very strong.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Maldives margin to recover as diesel prices ease and solar capacity comes online; Q3 and Q4 peak seasons expected to recoup the Q1 and Q2 fuel-driven decline (about INR15 crores impact).
Fuel costs in July were already about 26% below the April-May peak, per management.

India: solar capex (about INR60 crores, Pune) targeted for Q4 FY27 commissioning, expected to add 5-6% to India EBITDA (elsewhere cited as 4-5% margin increase); management expects margin uplift from Q1 next calendar year.

Same-store revenue up 10% and same-store EBITDA up 15% in the quarter, per management.

544322|2026-03.headline: Unimech Q4 FY26 net revenue recovered to ~Rs 82 crore (gross ~Rs 96-97 crore pre-tariff concession); FY26 net revenue ~Rs 240 crore, PAT ~Rs 63 crore.
544322|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as one of the strongest quarters of the year, with sequential recovery in aerospace tooling demand after tariff-related disruption eased from February. Q4 net revenue was ~Rs 82 crore and Q4 PAT ~Rs 26 crore; FY26 net revenue exceeded Rs 240 crore (gross Rs 257 crore) and PAT was ~Rs 63 crore, lower than last year. Order book as of May 2026 is ~Rs 314 crore consolidated including Hobel (~Rs 107 crore), and management guides Q1 FY27 revenue above Q4 FY26. Hobel Bellows acquisition closed in April 2026 and the Saudi JV with Kanoo Group is in set-up; neither contributed to FY26 consolidated numbers.

segments.name: Aero tooling (aero engine and airframe complex tooling)
segments.commentary: Contributed ~90% of revenue in Q4 FY26 and over 90% for FY26; tooling order book ~Rs 100 crore+, executed on a PO-to-PO basis over 4-6 months.

segments.name: Precision components and assemblies
segments.commentary: Contributed ~10% of revenue; ~200 first article inspections (FAIs) done in FY26 with target to double; early production orders received in calendar 2026.

segments.name: Nuclear
segments.commentary: Order wins ~Rs 87 crore to date, mainly EMCCR projects at Tarapur and Madras, expected to execute over 12-18 months; ~10 qualified semi-systems/sub-assemblies.

segments.name: Hobel Bellows (acquired April 2026)
segments.commentary: Metallic bellows, flexible tubing and precision assemblies; ~Rs 107 crore order book; not yet consolidated in Q4 and expected from Q1 FY27; ~12-month visibility; AS9100 certification planned over 6-9 months.

segments.name: Dheya (30% stake)
segments.commentary: DET-500 micro gas turbine reached up to 90% load in tests with 500+ minutes runtime; DET-200 certification underway; initial orders from Tier-1 defence suppliers for two test engines, potentially scaling to ~200 engines. Unimech is exclusive manufacturing partner.

guidance_outlook: Q1 FY27 revenue to surpass Q4 FY26 revenue (~Rs 82 crore net); management reiterated this as a baseline, but did not give a numerical FY27 guidance.
Consolidated EBITDA margin expected to be healthier than FY26's ~31%; management declined to give an exact number and cautioned that the Saudi JV could weigh on full-year margin.
Other income to be very moderate in FY27 as large funds have been deployed toward M&A.
Core business capex not expected to be very significant in FY27; Saudi JV capex to be large, with ~$30 million total joint investment (Unimech 51%), largely spent over first three years.
Working capital days may rise to 150-160 days over time.
Saudi JV expected to break even over a three-year horizon; revenue contribution possible in FY27 or, optimistically, by end of FY27.
Nuclear orders expected to execute particularly in H2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Over 150 CNC machines and other machines at Bangalore facility; no major machine additions in Q4 FY26.
Plant utilisation ~50%; management expects asset productivity to improve over 30-36 months.
Free trade warehousing zone (FTWZ) has all approvals; ICEGATE portal in final stage; customer inventory holding to focus on non-US territories.
Kanoo Unimech JV: Ministry of Investment (Saudi) approval received; facility and machine procurement in progress; pilot leadership onboarding.
Depreciation rising by ~Rs 7 crore per quarter after new facility commissioning.
demand_pricing: Demand improved after US tariff reduction in February; customer inventory rebuilding has resumed, per management.
Unimech absorbs ~5% tariff sharing on parts and tooling consumed in the US market; Q4 revenue net of tariff concessions was ~Rs 82 crore vs ~Rs 96-97 crore before concessions.
Management says no structural loss of aero tooling business despite an analyst's question on a customer insourcing MRO tooling.
Qualified SKU base approaching 6,000; new aerospace customer onboarded and more in pipeline.
Management said energy infrastructure maintenance and localisation in Saudi Arabia are creating opportunities for precision and repair-oriented manufacturing.

qa_highlights.question: Is Hobel AS9100 certified and how soon can aerospace cross-sell start?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans AS9100 certification over 6-9 months, followed by NADCAP approvals for bending, welding and detection; aerospace qualification takes 2-3 years or more.

qa_highlights.question: How will the Rs 450 crore acquisition be accounted for, and how will ROCE move?
qa_highlights.answer: Goodwill and intangibles will arise at consolidation and are not amortised; ROCE/ROE post-acquisition is 10-16% but expected to improve as the business scales. Standalone pre-acquisition ROCE was above 50%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nuclear order mix and execution timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Current nuclear orders are mainly EMCCR projects at Tarapur and Madras, expected to finish in 12-18 months; new tenders are pending and Unimech has more than 10 qualified sub-assemblies.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book stay flat ex-Hobel and is aero tooling weakening?
qa_highlights.answer: Ex-Hobel order book is ~Rs 200 crore+; nuclear grew to ~Rs 87 crore, tooling ~Rs 100 crore+, and precision parts are building up. Management sees no structural loss in tooling.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue baseline for FY27 and Q1 FY27 expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is targeting Q1 FY27 above Q4 FY26 and called Q4 a baseline, but gave no numerical guidance. Hobel and legacy business are expected to contribute growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue miss the Rs 90-100 crore Q4 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross Q4 revenue was ~Rs 96-97 crore within guidance; after tariff concessions net revenue was ~Rs 82 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Saudi JV capex and margin impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Total joint investment is ~$30 million (Unimech 51%), mostly capex and infrastructure over three years; JV may pull down full-year margins, but the overall margin profile is expected to be similar to FY26.

544322|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 71% YoY to about INR108 crore, with Hobel Bellows consolidated for two months and a 36.5% EBITDA margin.

PAT was about INR28 crore (24% margin), up 46% YoY, though other income of INR7 crore (vs INR15 crore in Q4 FY26) flatters the quarter less than in the prior quarter. Management guided Q2 to be stronger, with three months of Hobel and a heavier precision component (PCA) contribution in H2. Confirmed order book stood at about INR280 crore including Hobel, slightly lower QoQ, which management attributed to customer pull-ins; the company also signed a USD7.5 million five-year supply agreement with FACC Austria.

segments.commentary: Contributed approx. 76% of Q1 revenue; management said demand visibility is constructive for next quarter and is dominated by aero engine tooling. Tooling orders are largely PO-to-PO.

segments.commentary: Covers nuclear, semiconductor, aerospace and Hobel Bellows, making up the remaining 24% of revenue. Management expects a much heavier PCA-led contribution in H2 FY27; about 80% of qualified PCA parts are moving into serial production.

segments.name: Hobel Bellows
segments.commentary: Contributed 21% of Q1 revenue (about INR22 crore for two months). Management guides 15-20% growth for this business; AS9100 certification for Vizag facility targeted by Q4 FY27.

segments.commentary: Cumulative nuclear order wins of approx. INR87 crore, with about 50% of the existing order book to execute in FY27, mainly in H2.

Blended gross margin of 65% seen as sustainable for FY27.

Other income expected to be roughly half of Q1 level in Q2 onwards.

qa_highlights.question: Expected revenue growth and gross/EBITDA margin range for FY27, and capex needs?

qa_highlights.question: Tooling mix between engine and airframe, and growth from SKU expansion versus existing programmes?

qa_highlights.question: Where Unimech sits in the value chain across precision components and aerospace?

544333|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 total income INR250 crore (+41% YoY), EBITDA INR44 crore (+27%), margin 17.5%; company entering AI data-centre business via GScale (up to 51%).
544333|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of INR250 crore (+41% YoY), EBITDA of INR44 crore (+27%), PBT of INR36 crore (+26%) and PAT of INR26 crore (+26%), with EBITDA margin at 17.5%. Two strategic moves were announced: acquisition of up to 51% in GScale Energy (AI data-centre power, cooling and skid products) and a ~19% stake in GL Hakko Japan for ~INR71 crore, with a right to rise to 51%. Management guided core business revenue to ~INR1,200 crore (+40-50%) and GScale to ~INR250 crore in FY27. Many forward figures (GScale revenue, margins, FY28) were left unquantified and deferred to future guidance.

financial_highlights.change: post Q1 billing, before some Q2 billing
management targets below 200 days in FY27

financial_highlights.metric: Export share of revenue in Q1

segments.name: Core engineering (pharma, chemical, CDMO glass-lining)
segments.commentary: Guided to grow 40-50% in FY27 to ~INR1,200 crore; CDMO is ~50% of the unexecuted order book, balance pharma and chemicals. Management says it is moving to solutions sales, with no product-vs-turnkey split disclosed.

segments.name: GScale Energy (AI data-centre products and turnkey)
segments.commentary: Targeting ~INR250 crore revenue (management clarified revenue, not bookings) by end-FY27; five customers in advanced discussions (three global MNCs, two Indian). Expects 23-25% EBITDA margin and ~20% ROCE on ~INR500 crore investment; plant ~4 lakh sq ft, first phase operational by November.

segments.name: GL Hakko (Japan glass-lining technology partner)
segments.commentary: GL Hakko revenue ~INR200 crore; target INR400 crore in 2-3 years. Shell-and-tube glass-lining heat exchangers already being made in India (80% built in Japan, 20% finished locally); exports planned from FY28.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance ~INR1,450 crore (core ~INR1,200 crore plus GScale ~INR250 crore).
Core business growth guided at 40-50% for FY27, up from earlier 25-30% minimum; management excluded current order book from the change.
EBITDA margin to be maintained at 17-18% going forward; GScale margin expected 23-25%.
Working capital days to fall below 200 in FY27 (September-half expected), and GScale targeted at 100-150 days.
GScale data-centre projects targeted at 18-20 months versus 24-36 months industry typical; ROCE expected ~20%.
FY28 GScale and consolidated revenue guidance deferred ('we will guide soon'); no quantified margin expansion from semiconductor glass-lining yet.
capex_capacity: GScale has acquired ~4 lakh sq ft factory space; ~2 lakh sq ft in full execution with robotic equipment ordered from multiple countries, arriving by mid-September.
GScale operations targeted to start by November 2026; further 2 lakh sq ft (factories 3 and 4) to be added by December 2026.
Total GScale investment cited at ~INR500 crore.
Management said full-fledged manufacturing setup to be complete around March (2027).
Manufacturing mix: GScale to make 60-70% of equipment in-house and source the balance; management says this can be increased.
Semiconductor-grade glass-lining reactors: glass sourced from Japan, fabrication and glass spraying in India; no technology transfer agreement currently.
demand_pricing: Management cites India data-centre capacity of 1.8 GW expected to grow to ~10.2-10.5 GW by ~2030-31; investment of USD5-7 million per MW, of which ~65% is products and installation.
GScale has one big order from a top Indian client for semiconductor-related glass-lining reactors (GL Hakko-linked); pilot-plant order for LED/electronic chemicals also cited.
Shell-and-tube glass-lining heat exchanger price cut claimed: from ~INR30 lakh to ~INR12-15 lakh per unit (>50% lower), with management arguing it is a client benefit and margin-accretive.
India glass-lining TAM cited at ~INR1,500 crore; shell-and-tube heat exchanger TAM ~INR2,000 crore in India and ~USD2 billion globally.
Management claims no global competitor makes the GL Hakko shell-and-tube glass-lining heat exchanger or low-leaching glass; unverified.
Export share remained low at 2-3% in Q1 due to global uncertainty; shipping costs cited by an analyst as up ~4x.

qa_highlights.question: What is the GScale business, margins, and timing of order conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Brahma Reddy said five customers (three global MNCs, two Indian) are in LOI or near-order stage; target is ~INR250 crore revenue by end-FY27, clarified as revenue not order booking. Margin guided at 23-25% EBITDA.

qa_highlights.question: Margin expansion from semiconductor glass-lining products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will rise slightly as shell-and-tube and semiconductor products scale from September, but gave no quantified figure.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an unexecuted order book for core business?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, ~INR1,400 crore after Q1 billing, with some billing expected in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin down and is it structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the decline to mechanisation in two units, which reduced consumable consumption; employee costs rising with recruitment. Management said margins will be maintained at 17-18%.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital days and drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said days were ~320 last year, targeted below 200 by September, driven by customer advances and receivable collection with stock held flat.

qa_highlights.question: Royalty on imported technology?
qa_highlights.answer: No royalty currently; licensing model, with JV and technology-transfer discussions ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Data-centre project timelines and value-add?
qa_highlights.answer: Typical industry project 24-36 months; GScale targets 18-20 months. Customers may free-issue some long-lead items; the 60% in-house share can be increased.

Dependence on GL Hakko technology: critical glass manufacturing remains in Japan with no technology transfer agreement; GL Hakko stake to step up to 51% only on targets.
Forward guidance gaps: FY28 numbers for GScale and consolidated revenue not yet guided; a Q&A figure of ~INR3,000 crore for FY28 was not confirmed by management.
Customer concentration: GScale's five named-stage customers are unnamed; claims of no global competitor are unverified.

Margins? No. No.

544333|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and promotional on GScale and GL Hakko growth, with strong claims on uniqueness and market size. 544335|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 61% YoY to INR820 crore and PAT rose 77.8% to INR44.92 crore; order book stood at about INR1,235 crore at 31 March 2026.
544335|2026-03.overview: B.R.Goyal Infrastructure reported FY26 revenue from operations up 61% YoY to INR820 crore, with EBITDA (excluding other income) up about 82% to INR75 crore and EBITDA margin up 105 bps to 9.13%. H2 FY26 revenue was INR478 crore (up 61% YoY) with EBITDA of INR47.48 crore at a 9.93% margin. Management said the order book declined YoY to about INR1,235 crore, which it attributed to bidding for larger-ticket projects and faster execution. The company also flagged a preferential warrant issue of up to INR13.09 crore, higher borrowing limits, a maiden dividend of INR0.25 per share, and entry into wastewater civil works.

segments.name: EPC (roads, buildings, urban)
segments.commentary: Management cited an EPC EBITDA margin of about 14% for FY26 (13-15% range), up from 12-13% last year. FY26 revenue split by business: road/EPC about 49%, RMC about 3%, toll collection about 47%. Sector revenue cited: road/building EPC about INR395 crore, RMC about INR20 crore, wastewater about INR6 crore, toll about INR388 crore.

segments.name: Toll collection contracts (TCC)
segments.commentary: Toll EBITDA margin about 4% in FY26 (about 3% last year); management also cited a toll segment margin of about 2.5%. Toll strike rate is above 70%. Recent NHAI toll awards include Kathpur INR91.71 crore, Simliya INR86.7 crore, Aashpur INR70.39 crore, Khambara INR47.83 crore, Paraghat INR33.27 crore.

segments.name: Wastewater treatment
segments.commentary: Entered in FY26 with a Tamil Nadu project of about INR167 crore; wastewater order book about INR162 crore. Management cited a 15-20% EBITDA margin for the vertical, but work is currently subcontracted or on name-lending basis with no technology tie-up. Target contribution of 20-25% of revenue in the near future.

segments.name: Ready-mix concrete and real estate
segments.commentary: RMC revenue about INR20 crore in FY26. Residential plotting in Indore has about 1.8 lakh sq ft unsold inventory, with WIP/inventory about INR15 crore. The company also holds a 10% stake in Virtuoso Infra Meditech LLP, a Indore commercial real-estate build with about 3-3.5 lakh sq ft saleable area and expected revenue of about INR150 crore.

guidance_outlook: Management targets 20-25% revenue growth annually; for FY27 it aims for EBITDA margin of 10-11% against 9.13% in FY26 (about 9-9.25% blended in its margin discussion).
Top FY27 priority is order inflow of about INR2,000 crore, across roads, wastewater and toll contracts.
Bids of about INR1,500-2,000 crore are pending opening; about INR2,500 crore of orders identified for bidding in the current month.
Bid capacity cited at about INR2,000 crore; individual EPC bid capacity INR600-700 crore; building about INR150 crore; toll collection described as unlimited based on net worth.
Plans to bid PPP, HAM and BOT projects in the current fiscal, including NHAI asset monetisation of about 17 road projects.
Management said it would not commit to the projected INR1,000-1,200 crore of project completions in FY27.
capex_capacity: Equipment base of 230+ construction equipment and vehicles; workforce above 1,100 employees.
Operates 37 ongoing projects across nine states; executed more than 40 projects in total.
Preferential issue of convertible warrants up to INR13.09 crore approved; proceeds targeted at working capital needs in about 10-12 months.
Borrowing limits enhancement proposed to support larger projects.
Acquired 10% stake in Virtuoso Infra Meditech LLP (Indore real-estate build, completion in about 2-2.5 years).
demand_pricing: Management said tender flow has not slowed; the YoY order book decline reflects a shift to larger projects and faster execution of earlier orders, with about INR811 crore executed in FY26.
Strike rate: about 10-15% in EPC road building and above 70% in toll collection contracts.
Wastewater competition is intensifying: for a INR200 crore BUIDCO bid there were 15-20 bidders; the company was L2 in one and L3 in another bid.
Fuel and crude price volatility: force majeure and price-escalation clauses are being invoked; management says a short-term hit of about 1-1.5 months has since stabilised.
Company prefers centrally funded projects (NHAI, NHIDCL, MoRTH); working capital cycle cited at 30-45 days.
Company prefers large tickets: NH projects above INR500 crore and building projects above INR50 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the order book fall YoY, and is tender flow slowing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no slowdown; the company is bidding for larger projects and executed INR811 crore in FY26 against a INR1,313 crore opening order book. It said about INR1,500-2,000 crore has been bid and is not yet opened.

qa_highlights.question: What margin should investors expect going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Blended EBITDA margin is 9-9.25% currently; FY26 toll EBITDA was about 4% and EPC about 14%. Target for the current year is 10-11% blended.

qa_highlights.question: What is the wastewater margin, and how will mix evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Wastewater EBITDA margin was cited at 15-20%. Management expects wastewater at about 20-25% of revenue in the near future, with the balance from roads, buildings, RMC and toll. It is currently subcontracting or name-lending because it lacks credentials.

qa_highlights.question: How did FY26 growth split across business lines?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave FY26 revenue split of about 49% road, 3% RMC, 47% toll, with wastewater very small. Road and toll drove the growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company exposed to fuel price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts include force majeure and price-variation provisions; some agencies have issued SOPs, and the company expects price variations to offset the increase.

qa_highlights.question: What are the biggest opportunities and risks?
qa_highlights.answer: Opportunities cited are large TOT-model toll contracts of INR1,500-2,000 crore and the return of BOT projects. Execution risk remains, though management said it has 40 years of experience and works in nine states.

risks_watch: Order book fell YoY to about INR1,235 crore; conversion of about INR1,500-2,000 crore pending bids is key to FY27 growth.
Wastewater margin claims (15-20%) are unproven; the company lacks credentials and works as subcontractor or name-lender; competition is intense.
Management declined to commit to FY27 completions of INR1,000-1,200 crore, citing geopolitical and macro uncertainty.
Toll segment margin (about 2.5-4%) is much lower than EPC, so mix shift toward toll dilutes margin.
Operating cash flow was negative in FY25 and turned positive in FY26; sustainability is management's expectation, not guaranteed.
Management did not provide an order book figure as of 31 May 2026.
544335|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on growth and margin direction, but evasive on specifics: management declined to commit to FY27 project completion figures and offered inconsistent segment margin and revenue-mix figures. Answers on wastewater and PPP/HAM strategy were broad and aspirational.
key_quotes: Sir, we expect around a 20% to 25% growth rate, trying to maintain that.
So, we are trying to stay around 40% in EPC road and building from revenue.
We don't think we are conservative in out bidding we think we shouldn't unnecessarily have an order book of INR5,000 crores and then not be able to execute the work for 5, 10 years.

544339|2026-03.headline: Laxmi Dental Q4 FY26 revenue rose 21.9% YoY to Rs 74 crore with EBITDA margin at 18.3%, and FY26 revenue grew 16.2% to Rs 277.9 crore.
544339|2026-03.overview: Management described Q4 FY26 as a recovery quarter with highest-ever quarterly revenue of Rs 74 crore, up 21.9% YoY, and broad-based growth across dental lab, aligners and pediatric segments. EBITDA rose 41.8% YoY to Rs 13.5 crore and PAT reached Rs 10.1 crore, helped by a Rs 1.3 crore tax benefit tied to a labour code gratuity item. FY26 closed with revenue of Rs 277.9 crore, EBITDA of Rs 43.4 crore and PAT of Rs 28.9 crore, against a weak Q3. Management declined to give FY27 margin or growth guidance, and cited the company's Rs 99 crore cash balance and ongoing scanner deployment as strategic priorities.

vs Rs 4.3 crore in Q4 FY25; includes Rs 1.3 crore tax benefit
vs Rs 1.3 crore last year; company debt-free

segments.name: Dental lab (total)
segments.commentary: Record quarterly revenue of Rs 45.9 crore, up 27% YoY, with international lab up 40.9% YoY and domestic lab up 16.3% YoY to Rs 23.7 crore. Digital penetration in domestic lab is about 80%, with a medium-term target above 90%.

segments.name: Bizdent (domestic clear aligners)
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 10.9% YoY in Q4 after a sequential recovery; management said margins were prioritised over pricing, which had been under pressure in prior quarters.

segments.name: Vedia (aligner raw material, mainly export)
segments.commentary: Revenue of Rs 7.3 crore, stable sequentially. Some March shipments slipped to April because freight costs roughly doubled, and in some cases nearly tripled, which delayed revenue recognition.

segments.name: Kids-e-Dental (pediatric)
segments.commentary: Quarterly revenue of Rs 5.4 crore. International registrations are in progress, with some regulatory steps cleared; no firm timeline given.

segments.name: Scanners
segments.commentary: Scanner sales were 211 units in Q4 FY26 and 1,009 units in FY26. Scanners carry lower margins and weighed on consolidated gross margin in Q4.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 guidance. Management said it wants to do better than the 16.2% FY26 growth over the next two to three years, but did not endorse a 20% CAGR.

Management did not reaffirm the earlier target of 18-20% EBITDA margin, 75-80% gross margin and 13-15% PAT margin by FY27 or FY28. It said Q4 margins were in line with that range but would not give a timeline today.
Operating leverage is expected as people costs grow less than revenue; COGS will scale in proportion to sales. Automation and digital dentistry investments are planned.
Capex for FY27 will be set based on operational needs and revenue growth, funded from IPO proceeds still on hand.
US tariff is now about 10% (was about 50%). Management said this is not a deal breaker and expects US business to keep growing.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was about Rs 18.4 crore. FY27 capex will be balanced against operational capabilities and revenue growth, with no fixed amount given.
Scanner deployment remains a strategic priority: 211 units in Q4 FY26 and 1,009 units in FY26. Management wants to place as many as possible before scanners become commoditised.
Investment in automation and AI (AI Dent) continues to support cost structure and digital dentistry.
demand_pricing: Export share of revenue is about 33-34%. US is about 20% of revenue, and management said it is well diversified across customers, not dependent on Heartland Dental.
Management said the US tariff eased to about 10% from about 50%, and it absorbed higher tariff costs in the first half of Q4. It said the scale-up in the US was gradual and cautious.
Domestic aligner pricing was under pressure in prior quarters; management chose to protect margins, with Bizdent recovering in Q4.
Vedia orders were delayed by freight costs, but management said YoY growth is good and the business is not facing structural uncertainty.

The iScope 360 remote oral-health and aligner-monitoring product launched about two weeks before the call. It is sold through dentists at about Rs 2,000 retail with points-based subscription, and it may also be offered in export markets.
Competition is rising in domestic aligners and from funded players. Management said 22,000 dentists are active with Laxmi, against about 3 lakh dentists in India.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Bizdent revenue stay flat FY25 to FY26, and how much of the Q4 recovery came from pricing versus volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it chose to protect margins over price cuts during the pricing pressure. It did not split Q4 recovery between price and volume, and said it will keep balancing price against growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Vedia lower QoQ despite rupee depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight costs roughly doubled, and in some cases nearly tripled, which delayed March shipments into April. Management said YoY growth is good and there is no structural problem.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for the lab business run rate of about Rs 40-45 crore per quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it cannot give a number today, but expects growth in both domestic and international lab over the next two to three years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for margins and growth for FY27 and beyond?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give FY27 guidance. It said it wants to improve margins over the next two to three years and that Q3 was an exception. Q4 EBITDA margin was 18%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Heartland Dental's contract under review, and are more US DSOs coming?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there has been no change to the Heartland contract. It said more DSOs are being added but will not be announced individually, and that the business is diversified.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company considering acquisitions with its cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will evaluate opportunities that add value and will disclose them only once completed. It gave no specifics.

risks_watch: US tariff regime remains volatile. Current 10% rate could change, and the US is about 20% of revenue.
Freight costs and global shipping disruption caused Vedia export delays, which could recur at quarter-end.
Bizdent faces pricing pressure from domestic and funded competitors. Management is weighing margin against growth.
Gross margin is diluted by scanner sales, which carry lower margins. Scanner margin trajectory matters for consolidated margin.
Management has not reaffirmed the earlier margin targets. Watch whether FY27 margins hold at Q4 levels.
Kids-e-Dental international registration timing is uncertain.
Recent labour code changes affected Q3 gratuity and tax; Q4 PAT included a Rs 1.3 crore tax benefit that will not recur.

Scanner business is for us an enabler.

544339|2026-06.headline: Laxmi Dental Q1 FY27 revenue rose 13.9% y-o-y to about INR75 crore, a record, with EBITDA margin at 19.2% and PAT up 23.8%.
544339|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue, with consolidated revenue from operations of INR74.7 crore against INR65.6 crore a year earlier. Gross margin was 78.6% and EBITDA rose 20.6% y-o-y to INR14.4 crore at a 19.2% margin, helped by favourable mix and a scanner trading contribution. Dental lab grew 23.5% y-o-y, with international up 37.4%, while aligners grew 28.6%. Management flagged a new US CEO hire, a planned Palghar land purchase to replace rented facilities, and FY27 scanner deployment of 800 to 1,000 units. The company remains debt-free.

segments.name: Dental lab

segments.commentary: Grew 28.6% y-o-y. Bizdent grew 27.8% and Vedia grew 29.3%. Management linked growth to the iScope at-home monitoring launch and dentist education.

segments.name: Kids-e-Dental (paediatric)
segments.commentary: Grew 54.4% y-o-y in the quarter. The company holds 60% of its PAT in its adjusted EBITDA calculation.

qa_highlights.question: What differentiates Laxmi Dental products for dentists after the iScan Pro scanner, given no exclusive tie-ups?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 36 years of trust, global quality standards and ISO-certified systems, and innovation, and said it is the only branded crown player.

qa_highlights.question: What is scanner gross margin and how lumpy will margins be?
qa_highlights.answer: Scanners are a trading item with a 15% to 20% margin. Excluding scanners, margins are stable and rising; Q1 margin was 19.2% vs about 15% in the previous quarter and 18% a year ago.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity and utilisation for lab and aligners?
qa_highlights.answer: Aligners at about 70% utilisation. Lab runs at a constant 90% to 95% because of custom work.

qa_highlights.question: Why acquire Palghar land and will there be disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Goal is to move from two rented sites to one owned facility to cut about INR2 crore rent and gain room to expand. Management expects no revenue disruption.

qa_highlights.question: Why is domestic lab growing only about 12% and when will it improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was 12% y-o-y, attributed to satellite labs adding customer proximity, and expects faster growth from Q2 onwards.

544340|2026-03.headline: Rikhav Securities H2 FY26 PAT fell to INR1.20 crore (EPS 0.31) on cash-market investment losses; FY26 PAT INR18.96 crore.
544340|2026-03.overview: H2 FY26 total income was INR1,604 crore (as stated), EBITDA INR6.57 crore and PAT INR1.20 crore. FY26 total income was INR1,991 crore, EBITDA INR32.53 crore and PAT INR18.96 crore, with EPS of 4.95. Management attributed the weak profit to a loss of roughly INR18-23 crore on legacy cash-market equity investments, valuation losses at the 31 March 2026 market low, higher depreciation from about INR5.40 crore of technology spend, and an unrecognised SLBM profit of INR4.33 crore expected to be realised in coming quarters. Management is cutting cash-market exposure and SME inventory, and is building institutional broking, ETF market making and commodity arbitrage. Several answers were vague or deferred to email, and the call was disrupted by line dropouts.

segments.commentary: SME exposure was cut to about 30% of last year's level, roughly INR20-25 crore. Market making in ETFs has started with Kotak Mutual Fund, with two or three more mutual funds planned.

segments.name: Institutional broking
segments.commentary: Empanelled Kotak Mutual Fund, Bank of India and RBL Bank, and 8-10 FPIs have started. Management said real revenue will start next year and expects SBI and LIC empanelment.

segments.name: Commodities

Cash-market investments to be cut by INR50 crore, with a further INR50 crore cut planned; total cash-market deployment capped at about INR50 crore in FY27.

Plans to deploy AI-led audit and analytics in a regulated, human-vetted way; data gathering restricted to institutional clients for now.

Retail onboarding is 100% digital (e-KYC via a third-party vendor), with account-opening cost of INR60-70 and overall cost per account of about INR500.
Management said it charges the same brokerage as discount brokers and competes on dealer personal touch.
SEBI derivatives tariff circular: management sees a short-term hit to volumes and a long-term benefit as retail traders shift savings to investing.
Management said the retail and HNI participation recovery depends on a market revival.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the pressure on PAT and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a loss of INR18-20 crore on cash-market shares bought about 1.5 years earlier, unrealised SLBM profit of INR4-4.5 crore, about INR30 lakh more depreciation and INR75-80 lakh of tax adjustment.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SME share of inventory and value?
qa_highlights.answer: SME exposure is now about 30% of last year's level, around INR20-25 crore. Management said the whole stock is sold within a week of listing.

qa_highlights.question: Did the ~INR8-10 crore result hit come from valuation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about INR8-10 crore of the impact to valuation at 31 March, when Nifty was below 23,000 amid the US-Iran conflict.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cumulative technology investment and how is the stack split?
qa_highlights.answer: Cumulative spend is INR7.5-10 crore over two years. About 30-40% is in-house and about 50% goes to third-party vendors.

qa_highlights.question: Cybersecurity breaches and audits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no attempted breaches or disruptions this year. Trading endpoints get monthly audits, with a third-party listed entity doing reviews.

qa_highlights.question: Client base and ARPU?

qa_highlights.question: Digital CAC and retention?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said digital account-opening costs INR60-70 and total cost per account about INR500. No digital marketing has started yet, and relationship-based retention is about 100%.

qa_highlights.question: Commodity and accounting-change questions?

544340|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on long-term structure and technology, but defensive and vague on specifics such as the income jump, stock-in-trade purchases, SME exposure and guidance. Management deferred several questions to email and repeated the market-downturn explanation.
