Institutional is a, just we have empanelled and we have just started, and this also, this year also most of the part we will, our time goes on for the empanelling the institution, good institution.

544342|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 14.4% to INR 434.12 crore and PAT 35.61% to INR 43.84 crore; management reiterates 30-35% CAGR target.
544342|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 total revenue of INR 434.12 crore (+14.4% YoY), EBITDA of INR 61.35 crore (+23.34%) and PAT of INR 43.84 crore (+35.61%), against an internal target of INR 430 crore revenue and INR 40 crore PAT. The Bhilwara 10,000 MT R-32 plant received environmental clearance and is guided to start production by October 2026. Q4 revenue of about INR 110 crore was flat-to-down versus prior quarters, which analysts questioned; management attributed this to LPG and energy disruptions hitting end-customer industries. Management reiterated 30-35% revenue CAGR and 3-4% margin improvement over three years, with FY27 PAT guided at about INR 100 crore and a 2030 aspiration of INR 3,000 crore revenue and INR 500 crore PAT.

segments.name: Fluorochemicals / refrigerants (R-32, HFO blends)
segments.commentary: Management said R-32 prices are INR 800-900/kg currently versus its INR 500-550/kg planning assumption; the company has largely exited domestic R-32 sales (from over 4,500 MT two years ago to 400-500 MT now) due to low margins.

segments.name: Specialty and high-purity gases (helium, semiconductor gases)
segments.commentary: Khalapur helium plant is in final testing with start-up expected next month (around June 2026); helium prices reportedly moved from INR 800-900 to above INR 3,000-4,000 per unit as cited by management, with supply tightness from Qatar.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR target of 30-35% over next three years with margin improvement of 3-4%.

FY27 revenue: management cited about INR 275 crore from R-32 over six months of operation plus the existing business, implying about INR 430 crore base; FY27 PAT estimated at about INR 100 crore (40 crore base plus about 60 crore from new capacity at 22% PAT).
H1 FY27 PAT margins expected to be similar to last year's levels; H2 margins expected to rise about 5-6 percentage points as manufacturing (22-24% PAT margin) contributes about 50% of growth.
Long-term aspiration by 2030: INR 3,000 crore revenue and INR 500 crore PAT; with R-32 fully operational, revenue should cross INR 1,100-1,200 crore with about INR 180 crore PAT.
HFO manufacturing plant (capex cited as INR 200 crore in MoU, stated as pure plant and machinery; total capex about INR 400 crore) to start only after Bhilwara stabilises, post mid-FY27.
capex_capacity: Bhilwara, Rajasthan: 10,000 MT R-32 plant; environmental clearance received; production expected by October 2026; capital work in progress about INR 35 crore, with management saying payments will rise as equipment is delivered (20-30% advances, 70% on delivery, 30% on commissioning).
Khalapur, Maharashtra: helium and liquid helium/semiconductor gas facility in final testing; start-up expected around June 2026.

Mumbattu, Andhra Pradesh: South India facility for HFO/HFC blending, de-bulking, helium and semiconductor gas handling; scaled from an IPO plan of 5 bulk tanks to 12 tanks; operational by August 2026 per management.
HFO manufacturing plant: management said to start after Bhilwara is stabilised (post mid-FY27); no further dilution envisaged after the rights issue.
Company operates four facilities with two more under development, supported by a pan-India distribution network.
demand_pricing: R-32 prices currently INR 800-900/kg (bulk), roughly double earlier levels; other products up about 15-20% per management.
Management expects Indian refrigerant/air-conditioning demand to grow 10-15% YoY for the next 10 years; Indian market for R-32 cited at 20,000-22,000 MT.
Industry capacity: management cited about 40,000-50,000 MT of additional R-32 capacity coming up in India, designed largely for exports; China HFC capacity cited at about 800,000 MT.
Q4 top-line flat-to-lower attributed to LPG shortages and supply-chain disruption hitting end-customer industries rather than pricing.
Quota: management expects 10,000 MT quota allocation for the Bhilwara plant; government policy expected in FY27, details not yet released.
No pre-contracts or offtake agreements signed for R-32; management said it sees no need for tie-ups at this stage.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the rights entitlement sold rather than applied for, and why has shareholding fallen?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said shares sold were bought back, and the dilution (about 68%) reflected an issue price of INR 99 rather than the INR 140 initially planned; current holding stated at about 47.5% or a little more.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30-35% growth target on track given FY26 growth of 14% and a sharp QoQ revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target was INR 430 crore revenue and INR 40 crore PAT for FY26, which was surpassed; 30-35% growth is for the next three years; FY27 needs about INR 560 crore for 30% growth and is expected to exceed it if R-32 starts on time.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timing and revenue contribution from Khalapur and Mumbattu, and the HFO plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Khalapur start-up expected around June; Mumbattu by August; no separate revenue figure given for these sites. HFO plant to start after Bhilwara is stabilised, post mid-FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Bhilwara CWIP only about INR 35 crore against a roughly INR 200 crore capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Company pays 20-30% advances only, with balance on delivery and commissioning; orders placed for almost all equipment, so payments should rise significantly this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Saudi helium tie-up and Qatar disruption affect sourcing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Sharjah Oxygen tie-up is strategic; Qatar helium output is curtailed, but helium prices have risen sharply, which management views as an opportunity.

qa_highlights.question: What are FY27 PAT margins and the assumed R-32 price?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 FY27 margins similar to prior year; H2 up about 5-6 points; FY27 PAT about INR 100 crore based on INR 500-550/kg R-32 pricing, below the current INR 900/kg.

risks_watch: Commissioning delays at Bhilwara (October 2026), Khalapur and Mumbattu; analysts noted a possible one-to-two month slip, which management said higher prices could offset.
Government R-32 quota allocation (10,000 MT assumed) not yet released; policy expected in FY27.
Q4 revenue of about INR 110 crore versus INR 150 crore in the prior-year quarter; management attributes this to LPG and energy disruption affecting customers.
Margin pressure in H1 FY27 from higher oil and LPG costs; management said margins 'would be highly strained'.

Shareholding dilution and rights issue execution; analyst questioned consistency of rights application commitments.
Management's use of unaudited growth targets and differing capex figures (INR 200 crore vs INR 400 crore total); guidance clarity to be monitored.

544342|2026-06.headline: Stallion Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12.78% YoY to ₹124.68 crore while PAT jumped 79.15% to ₹18.57 crore; management says margins are partly one-off.
544342|2026-06.overview: Revenue reached ₹124.68 crore (+12.78% YoY), EBITDA rose 75.85% to ₹25.27 crore and PAT rose 79.15% to ₹18.57 crore. Management attributed the margin jump to a mix of better product mix (higher HFO share), earlier logistics planning and inventory gains, splitting EBITDA roughly 50:50 between inventory gains and operations. The high-purity helium plant at Khalapur (1,200 MTPA) is complete with commercial operations expected next quarter, while the 10,000 MT R32 plant at Bhilwara slipped from a July 2026 target to end-December 2026, and Mambattu (HFO blending) is now due by year-end. Management reiterated 30-35% revenue CAGR guidance but cut the FY27 contribution expectation from the R32 plant and opened the door to dilution or debt for expansion.

financial_highlights.metric: EBITDA margin (analyst-cited, not stated by management)
financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY27 level as referenced in Q&A

segments.name: Specialty gases - High-purity helium (Khalapur)
segments.commentary: 1,200 MTPA plant ready; commercial operations expected next quarter. Management guides ~5 containers in FY27, rising to 12 in FY28 and 24 thereafter; contribution about 12% of revenue this year per management. Availability of supply, not selling, is the constraint.

segments.name: Refrigerants - R32 (Bhilwara)
segments.commentary: 10,000 MT plant, completion now targeted end-December 2026 (earlier July 2026, then March 2027 startup per funding delay). Management now expects ~₹125 crore revenue in Q4 FY27 and says FY27 contribution will 'change a little bit' from ₹250 crore; FY28 ₹500-600 crore reiterated. Current R32 price ~₹800/kg vs ~₹900 peak; guidance based on ₹550/kg.

segments.name: HFO blending (Mambattu, Andhra Pradesh)
segments.commentary: Now expected by year-end versus earlier August target; scope expanded to 12 tanks with hydrocarbon and helium capability. Management says immediate turnover uplift may be only ~10%, with margin benefit larger.

segments.commentary: About 50% of business; management says conventional business earns roughly 10% PAT margin, with new businesses at ~24% PAT.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of 30-35% maintained over next three years; management says 'the 30-35% is intact'.
EBITDA margin expected to improve by about 3-4% over the medium term as backward integration and specialty gases scale.

Peak revenue target above ₹1,100 crore in FY28 with helium, R32 and Mambattu fully operational, at ~15% PAT minimum (per analyst's framing, confirmed by management).
Long-term target of ₹3,000 crore revenue; plan of roughly one new plant per year for three years, with timeline could stretch to six years without external funding.
Capex for proposed HFO plant estimated at ₹350-400 crore for 10,000 tons capacity; management to announce more toward end of year after R32 commissioning.
capex_capacity: Khalapur high-purity helium: 1,200 MTPA installed, commercial ops expected next quarter.
Bhilwara R32: 10,000 MT; target completion end-December 2026 (previously July 2026). Delay attributed to funding: preferential issue abandoned, rights issue funding arrived late (February).
Mambattu (AP): HFO blending plant, expected operational by end-2026; scope enlarged to 12 tanks from 5 with hydrocarbon/helium capability, requiring redesign.
Proposed HFO plant: 10,000 tons (5,000+5,000), capex ₹350-400 crore; technology transfer payment already incurred; EC approval takes ~6 months; announcement expected toward year-end.
Management says capex is within budget with no overspend.
demand_pricing: Helium: price rose sharply over past 6-7 months and is now stable at ~₹4,000/kg per management (approximate). HFO realisations cited at ~₹3,000-4,000/kg for the two grades to be manufactured.
Management says imports of R32 have fallen to almost negligible; own R32 volumes will be incremental, not substitutive, revenue.
AHF (raw material): management expects a glut by 2028 with buyer's market conditions; multiple domestic and global sources, with plans for more than one supplier per critical input.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the margin expansion is pricing vs product mix, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a combination of better product mix (higher HFO share), earlier logistics planning and high stock-keeping during the Gulf crisis; said inventory gains are roughly 50:50 of EBITDA, and that margins will not necessarily repeat.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30-35% revenue growth guidance still intact after the R32 delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said the 30-35% is intact, while acknowledging the FY27 R32 contribution will change slightly from ₹250 crore; Q4 R32 revenue expected around ₹125 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the R32 plant delayed and what funding was used?
qa_highlights.answer: A planned preferential issue was abandoned after a share-price spike; a rights issue was used instead, reaching the market only by February, so the planned December startup slipped to March-end under the original plan.

qa_highlights.question: What are the helium volumes and how is supply secured given Middle East shipping disruption?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects ~5 containers in FY27, 12 in FY28, 24 after; utilisation about 20% of 1,200 MTPA next year. Supply secured via Sharjah Oxygen, swap arrangements and multiple sources; price expected to rise.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise equity or debt for the expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it previously preferred internal accruals, but now sees dilution and debt as likely for faster growth ('some dilution, some debt, not all debt'); no decision made yet.

qa_highlights.question: How much R32 volume is pre-sold under contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose pre-sales, calling existing understandings non-enforceable MOUs; said the company will not commit to take-or-pay contracts ahead of plant readiness.

risks_watch: R32 Bhilwara completion slipped from July 2026 to end-December 2026 after funding delays; FY27 R32 contribution (earlier ₹250 crore) expected to change, with Q4 FY27 revenue around ₹125 crore; watch for further slippage and commissioning updates next quarter.
Q1 FY27 margins described by management as a special quarter, with about 50% of EBITDA from inventory gains; FY27 PAT margin ex-R32 seen around 10%, so margin normalisation is a key risk.

R32 pricing downtrend (about ₹800/kg vs ~₹900 peak) against guidance based on ₹550/kg; no contracted or take-or-pay offtake disclosed for R32 volumes, with management calling existing understandings non-enforceable MOUs.
Mambattu scope expanded to 12 tanks and now due by year-end; HFO plant (₹350-400 crore, 10,000 tons) pending EC approval of about six months, with announcement expected towards year-end.

Now we are close to the idea that we might go for dilution onwards.
We would go public I think towards the end of the year after this plant is successfully commissioned is when we would go in full swing for the HFO plant, not before.

Notably evasive on pre-sold R32 volumes and on the AHF raw-material source, and more open than before on the possibility of dilution and debt.

544343|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue from operations rose to INR105.05 crore (from INR99.7 crore), with EBITDA flat at INR35.80 crore and FY27 guidance of minimum 35% growth.
544343|2026-03.overview: FY26 total income grew 9.4% to INR115.60 crore and revenue from operations rose to INR105.05 crore, which management said was below internal expectations as enterprise decision cycles elongated and large ramp-ups slipped into FY27. EBITDA was INR35.80 crore versus INR35.69 crore, with the margin (31%, computed on total income including other income of about INR10.55 crore) moderating on Middle East investments, Gurgaon expansion, senior hires and AI build-out. PAT fell to INR25.50 crore from INR25.80 crore and basic EPS to INR10.44 from INR11.83, partly on a full-year post-IPO share count. The company remains debt-free with about INR171.3 crore of cash and investments, and announced a proposed acquisition of Epitome Cloud Inc. for about INR40 crore.

vs INR25.80 crore in FY25; PAT margin 22.1%
mainly FD interest and sale of current investments
cash and bank INR88.62 crore, current investments INR81.13 crore, LT FDs approx. INR1.6 crore

segments.commentary: AI-related revenue exceeded 10% of total company revenue for the first time in FY26. Management said all AI contracts start as fixed-cost discovery and move to T&M on production.

segments.commentary: US approx. 41%, Europe and UK approx. 31%, Middle East approx. 11%, India approx. 10%, rest of world approx. 7%. Management has pulled back Middle East trade-show spend and new-logo acquisition for now.

segments.name: Engagement model
segments.commentary: About 91% of FY26 revenue came from time-and-material engagements; the remaining about 9% was limited-period fixed-cost work.

EBITDA margin to recover gradually toward 33%, with management also referring to at least 200 bps improvement; the margin basis includes other income.
Three-year goal of about INR200 crore top line while maintaining and improving the EBITDA margin.

demand_pricing: Client retention about 90%; management expects about 10% churn and net new revenue of INR20-25 crore organically in FY27.
Two Fortune 500 wins in FY26 (life sciences/healthcare with domain analytics and warehouse management; chemicals and materials with UiPath automation).
Nine international trade shows in FY26, six in the Middle East; about 500 qualified leads generated, and deal cycles of 6-12 months mean conversions are still pending.

Middle East: one of the top five clients is in the region, with BFSI as the only vertical there; the company is holding off on net new logos in the region.
Management cited global economic uncertainty as the biggest sector headwind, plus AI talent availability; it cited increasing demand for AI, cloud modernisation and automation.

qa_highlights.question: Why has organic growth been weak, and what is the acquisition cost and contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Epitome is about INR40 crore consideration, INR28-30 crore revenue, and 25-30% of revenue contribution. Organic growth of INR20-25 crore net new is expected after about 10% churn; 35% is the most pessimistic case.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EBITDA margin 31% when the reported EBITDA is about INR25 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO confirmed the margin uses total income including other income (about INR10.55 crore) as the denominator. Excluding other income the EBITDA margin is about 34%, so the reported 31% is on the total-income basis.

qa_highlights.question: Why were trade-show and marketing costs reduced, and why did other expenses rise about 30%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Middle East trade-show commitments were cut because of the West Asia situation and spend was redirected to demand gen, US/UK/Europe events. Other expenses rose because Middle East staff are supplied via a third party (technical fees) and marketing spend was reallocated, not cut.

qa_highlights.question: What are the parameters for M&A and Epitome's margin effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described four criteria: services company with some IP, majority export revenue, profitable and growing, and a technology or domain specialisation. The CFO said targets must have EBITDA margins in line with the company and bring synergy and new technology or manpower. Management said margins would improve post-deal.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there no buyback given the cash position, and what is the dividend policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no buyback is planned for now, with capital directed to growth and acquisitions. The CFO said the dividend payout is intended to be about 20-25% of profit, including the final dividend, and a buyback may be reconsidered in about a year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 target breakdown and the three-year plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 35% is a combined organic and inorganic guidance and a three-year aim of INR200 crore top line with a stable or better margin. The CFO said the 'medium term' reference meant one year, for which 35% growth is projected.

risks_watch: Organic growth: FY26 growth was largely from pricing and the Middle East; FY27 depends on INR20-25 crore net new revenue and the slipped large ramp-ups.
Epitome integration: completion in 8-12 weeks and a Salesforce revenue-operations niche with only 7 onsite US staff; the EBITDA impact and the PAT contribution are not disclosed.
Margin: the 33% FY27 target includes other income, so operating margin is lower (about 24% ex-other income per an analyst's calculation); other income of INR10.55 crore is a large share of PBT.
Middle East: the top-five client exposure with teams no longer travelling; BFSI concentration.

544443|2026-03.headline: Travel Food Services Q4 system-wide sales grew 27.7% YoY to INR9 billion, while FY26 adjusted consolidated PAT rose 21.5% to INR4.5 billion on about 1% traffic growth.
544443|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a disruption-heavy year (India-Pakistan conflict, aircraft crash-related schedule cuts, FDTL crew rest curbs, Middle East conflict from March 2026) in which TFS airport passenger traffic grew only 1.2%. Despite this, system-wide sales grew 25.4% to INR32.1 billion, driven by 9.4% like-for-like growth and 13.1% net contract gains. Q4 saw gross margin of 87.3% (85.6% after a one-time reclassification) and EBITDA up 38.3%, but PAT growth was held to about 15% by a INR212 million litigation provision and a weaker JV contribution. Trade receivables rose to about INR2.64 billion at year-end on EATS ramp-up, which management expects to normalise by H1 FY27.

Annual dividend of INR10.25 per share for FY26, subject to shareholder approval.

qa_highlights.answer: Management did not guide numbers; cited 11 airports in the privatisation pipeline and said Kolkata's inclusion or state changes are not expected to alter the schedule.

qa_highlights.question: Can airport F&B pricing and energy costs be passed on?

qa_highlights.question: Are airport concession fees rising and what is long-term economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Rentals are a normal portfolio negotiation with some going up and some down; management said nothing dramatically different is happening.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost rise, and what drove the receivables increase?

qa_highlights.question: What is the steady-state LFL breakup?

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation and interest in duty-free or retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Management stressed cash discipline, zero debt and ROCE of about 45%, and prioritised international lounges and expressway wayside amenities; no duty-free plans were mentioned.

544444|2026-03.headline: Glen Industries H2 FY26 PAT of INR8.20 crore on INR108.60 crore income; management targets INR500 crore turnover and INR90 crore EBITDA in FY28.
544444|2026-03.overview: FY26 total income was INR205.16 crore, EBITDA INR38.50 crore and PAT INR16.50 crore, with H2 FY26 income of INR108.60 crore, EBITDA INR18.69 crore and PAT INR8.20 crore. Management attributed margin compression from about 23-24% in FY25 to about 18-19% in FY26 to passing on PLA price benefits to customers. A capacity expansion (plastic food containers roughly 3x, plus about 750 MT paper-based food packaging including paper cups) has a revised project cost of INR130-135 crore, now expected to start commercial production from September 2026. Raw material prices rose sharply after the West Asia conflict, with polypropylene peaking near INR150/kg and now about INR135/kg.

Normalized PAT nearly tripled YoY to INR 39 crores. Growth was supported by mature-centre occupancy (committed 92%) and a higher share of 1,000+ seat clients, GCCs and multi-city clients, though overall occupancy dipped to 81% from 82% QoQ as new centres filled up. Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance (28-30% revenue growth, 19-20% normalized EBITDA margin, 13 million sq ft by March 2027) and started a heavy capex cycle of INR 550-600 crores for the year.

qa_highlights.question: How is the 28-30% guidance built, given the existing base is at 92% committed occupancy?

Operating EBITDA was INR33 crores (11.4% margin) against reported EBITDA of INR36 crores. Order on hand stood at INR1,053 crores (up about 25% YoY), though Q1 order inflow of about INR260 crores was softer, which management attributed to large inquiries slipping into Q2. Freight costs (US-bound, roughly 2x to 2.5x since March) and steel prices (up 10-12%) are compressing margins, so management reiterated the 25%+ FY27 revenue growth target but declined to give a margin guide until Q3.

financial_highlights.change: Export ~1,400 MT vs ~INR3 crores in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR1,053 crores (Phenix INR837 crores, Proflex INR216 crores)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1.19 lakh YoY; vs INR1.38 lakh QoQ

segments.name: Phenix (PEB and heavy structural steel)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR214 crores, up 22% YoY; order book INR837 crores including export orders of INR278 crores to be executed mostly in FY27, about 28% dispatched to date. Sanand running at 75-80% utilisation.

segments.name: Proflex (self-supported steel roofing)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR77 crores, up 25% YoY; order book INR216 crores. Installed capacity raised to 21 lakh sq m per annum after commissioning two mobile manufacturing units.

segments.commentary: Export revenue INR28 crores (about 1,400 MT); management guides about 15% sustainable export EBITDA at current freight, 16-18% in normal freight, versus about 11% domestic. More than 8,000 MT expected in the remaining three quarters.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth of over 25% in FY27, implying about INR1,600 crores top line.
No specific FY27 margin guidance; management targets improvement over the current 11-11.5% operating EBITDA margin but will guide at Q2 results (next quarter).
Sanand 20,000 TPA brownfield expansion (PEB capacity 72,000 to 92,000 TPA) commissioning in October 2026, benefits in Q3-Q4 FY27.
Cheyyar brownfield expansion of 20,000 TPA to start this fiscal, completion Q3 FY28; total capacity about 1,54,000-1,55,000 TPA.
Over 20% CAGR over the next three to four years in the medium-term plan, with progressive profitability improvement.
Targeted PEB volume of 85,000-90,000 MT in FY27 versus 72,000 MT last year.
capex_capacity: Sanand PEB brownfield: +20,000 TPA, commissioning October 2026; PEB capacity to 92,000 TPA.

INR30 crores fully automated heavy structural steel processing line at Sanand, adding 10,000 tons to existing 12,000 tons; operational by Q1 FY28. Board approved an additional heavy structural expansion at Sanand.

Proflex installed capacity 21 lakh sq m per annum after two mobile manufacturing units.
2.5 MW ground-mounted captive solar plant in Gujarat under development.
Third plant site under evaluation in North India; to be announced once finalised.
demand_pricing: Q1 order inflow about INR260 crores; management says large inquiries have rubber-banded into Q2. Management cites an INR4,000 crore Phenix inquiry pipeline and about INR200 crores in Proflex.
Hit rate of 12-15% over the last five years, with a stated policy of protecting margins over chasing volume; peers reportedly near 20%.
60-70% of customers are repeat customers.
Freight costs to US roughly 2-2.5x March levels (USD10,000-12,000 per 40ft container); US Section 232 duty cut from 50% to 25%; US steel up about 10-12% since March; domestic freight up 2-5%.
Roughly 80-85% of raw material is booked at order booking; 15-20% is left open to price variation. Domestic PEB margins down 1-2% due to inflation.
Management says domestic market share is about 10-12%, targeting 15% over time.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q1 order inflow weak at about INR260 crores versus the INR100 crore/month run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Malav Patel said inflow was up 25% YoY; large inquiries took longer on design freeze and have rubber-banded into Q2. Management says the run rate of about INR100 crores of PEB per month is maintained.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export margin and how much does freight affect it?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Majmudar said the balance INR278 crores export order book yields about 15% EBITDA at peak freight, 16-17% in a better scenario; domestic is about 11%, so the gap has narrowed to about 4-5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Phenix realisation per MT fall QoQ to INR1.25 lakh from INR1.38 lakh?
qa_highlights.answer: Keyur Shah attributed it to export mix (under 10%) and project-specific bought-out items, not price cuts; management expects full-year comparability.

qa_highlights.question: Why was domestic PEB realisation flat despite higher steel prices?
qa_highlights.answer: Keyur Shah said domestic tonnage rose about 6.6% and revenue 7.6%; raw material cost was about 0.5% lower YoY and product mix (primary vs sheeting) drove the gap. Higher steel costs will show in orders booked at current prices.

qa_highlights.question: Will Cheyyar capacity come in Q1/Q2 FY28 or Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Malav Patel said the Cheyyar 20,000 TPA expansion comes in Q3 FY28, giving two effective quarters in FY28; Sanand's additional capacity arrives in Q3-Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 margin outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined a specific range, saying it will give guidance after one more quarter; the target is to improve over the current 11-11.5% operating margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the win rate on bids?
qa_highlights.answer: Chirag Patel said the win rate is 10-12%, up to 12-15% depending on order; large customers take longer to finalise engineering.

risks_watch: FY27 margin guidance deferred to Q2 results; management says it will give specific guidance only after one more quarter, so the 11-11.5% operating EBITDA base is the only reference point for now.

Freight and US tariff exposure: US-bound freight roughly 2-2.5x March levels (USD10,000-12,000 per 40ft container) with management saying freight is unlikely to be sustainable, yet pass-through is incomplete; export margin guided at about 15% at peak freight vs 16-18% normal.

Order inflow pacing: Q1 inflow about INR260 crores; large inquiries have slipped into Q2. Watch whether the roughly INR100 crore per month run rate is maintained against a INR4,000 crore Phenix pipeline and a 12-15% historical hit rate.

Capacity ramp timing: Sanand 20,000 TPA expansion due October 2026 (benefits Q3-Q4 FY27); Sanand heavy structural line by Q1 FY28; Cheyyar 20,000 TPA expansion in Q3 FY28. Any slippage would constrain the 25%+ revenue target and the 85,000-90,000 MT PEB volume goal.

Raw material pass-through: about 80-85% of steel is booked at order booking, with domestic PEB margins already down 1-2% from inflation. Management expects higher steel costs to show up in fresh orders, so the lag between price and margin needs tracking.
Export order execution: INR278 crore export order book to be executed over the next three quarters, about 28% dispatched so far; more than 8,000 MT expected in the remaining quarters of FY27.
key_quotes: While our objective is to improve margins on a full year basis, given the continuing uncertainty on the cost front rising from the West Asia crisis, we would prefer to wait for at least one more quarter before providing specific margin guidance for the year.
So, I will not run after orders just to make my hit rate 20% by letting go of my margins.
But at the same time, I am repeating myself that it will not come at the cost of my bottom line or my margin targets, Meaning both have to go hand in hand.
Sanjay Majmudar: Yes, 100%. Sir, we are talking of improving from 11% to 11.5%. There's no question. Blended margin, I am talking, okay?
544470|2026-06.management_tone: Management is confident on top-line growth (25%+ FY27 guidance, INR4,000 crore pipeline, 60-70% repeat customers) but cautious on margins, declining to give a FY27 margin number until Q2 because of freight and steel cost volatility tied to the West Asia situation. Answers on the hit rate and capacity were firm and strategy-led, while the explanation of Q1 realisation and order inflow was defensive, attributing both to timing, mix and rubber-banded inquiries rather than pricing.

544471|2026-03.headline: H2 FY26 revenue fell to Rs 28.97 crore with 5.32% EBITDA margin as management deferred loss-making fixed-price contracts amid component inflation.
544471|2026-03.overview: Takyon reported H2 FY26 (Oct 2025 to Mar 2026) consolidated revenue of Rs 28.97 crore, EBITDA of Rs 1.61 crore (5.32% margin) and PAT of Rs 0.44 crore. Full-year FY26 revenue was Rs 71.05 crore, EBITDA Rs 7.09 crore (near 10%), PAT Rs 3.65 crore and EPS Rs 3.29. H1 FY26 revenue was Rs 42.08 crore with EBITDA margin near 13%. Management attributed the H2 shortfall to component price inflation and lengthened lead times, and said it chose to defer unviable fixed-price contracts and protect the balance sheet. Total liabilities fell from Rs 50 crore to Rs 12.20 crore and trade payables from Rs 30.21 crore to Rs 3.77 crore.

financial_highlights.change: c.31% lower than FY25 per analyst question; not disputed by management
down from Rs 50 crore, c.75% reduction
management says lowest in peer group

segments.name: Supply and installation (fixed-price, largely)
segments.commentary: Of the Rs 32 crore confirmed order book, about Rs 20 crore is supply and installation, largely fixed-price from last year; OEM prices are reportedly frozen for these contracts. Management says escalated prices were built into bidding for new contracts.

segments.name: Services (O&M)
segments.commentary: About Rs 12 crore of the order book is operation and maintenance services, contracted quarterly.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue expected to be meaningfully higher than FY26; management says it will surpass FY24-FY25 levels by close to 15% (also referenced 15-20% growth on a Rs 100 crore baseline) and called FY26's Rs 71 crore not a new base.
H1 FY27 target: chasing at least a repeat of H1 FY26 revenue of Rs 42 crore.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at around 11-13% for the full year; management declined to forecast H1 margin given expected turbulence for the next 3-4 months.
Of the Rs 32 crore order book, Rs 27-28 crore expected to be billed; Rs 20-22 crore expected to be billed in H1 FY27; Rs 4-5 crore of multi-year revenue to spill over 2-3 years.
Management said no point-specific revenue guidance is provided.
Target customer mix in 2-3 years: 30% state governments, 40% PSUs, 30% enterprise (currently 85% government, 15% enterprise; government split c.60% state / 40% PSU).
capex_capacity: Confirmed executable order book of Rs 32 crore as on 31 March 2026, with fresh orders of Rs 3.2 crore received in the following 45 days.
Average project cycle of 4 to 5 months from bidding through procurement, supply and payment.

Supply lead times for certain critical IT hardware stretched from 8-12 weeks to 9-52 weeks; management said vendors were giving only 30-day price validity and the company declined to bid such projects.
Management expects component turbulence to last 3-4 more months per OEM and industry feedback.
Geographic expansion: senior technical-commercial hire in Mumbai for BFSI customers; continued focus on North East (Assam, Tripura and other seven sister states).
demand_pricing: Component prices for switches, firewalls, compute and storage rose 40% to over 300% in some items, per management, attributed to AI data-centre demand absorbing global manufacturing capacity.
Management says no customers or market share were lost in H2; one Rs 5 crore services contract ended and was re-entered into the bidding process, with re-entry expected in June.
Company is pursuing BFSI (previously minimal in book) and DPDP Act compliance awareness with existing customers; no DPDP order book visibility yet.
Mitigation: diversified vendors, added price escalation clauses to new contracts, locked better supplier visibility, and shifted procurement toward Make in India product lines.

Management cited peers Allied Digital (standalone swung from Rs 10 crore profit to net loss in FY26) and Tejas Networks (revenue down 82% in Q4 FY26) as evidence of margin damage from chasing revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the current order book and any FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book Rs 32 crore as of 31 March 2026, with Rs 3.2 crore new orders in the following 45 days; no point revenue guidance, but FY27 expected meaningfully above FY26 and about 15% above FY24-FY25 levels.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is fixed price?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 20 crore supply and installation (largely fixed-price) and Rs 12 crore quarterly O&M services; management says OEMs have frozen prices on current fixed-price orders, so no further escalation in the existing book.

qa_highlights.question: Was the H2 shortfall supply chain or execution-related?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no execution failures, project cancellations or quantitative losses; the shortfall was due to price inflation and supply disruption.

qa_highlights.question: What is the government vs non-government mix and target?
qa_highlights.answer: Currently 85% government and 15% enterprise, with government split about 60% state and 40% PSU; target in 2-3 years is 30% state, 40% PSU, 30% enterprise.

qa_highlights.question: Why will supply constraints normalise in 3-4 months?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this reflects OEM and industry feedback that current orders now carry firm timelines of 3-4 months; it said the company had not forecast a 3-4 month normalisation as a fixed number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided FY27 full-year EBITDA margin to 11-13%, having delivered close to 10% in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY26 revenue a new base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no, FY26 is not a baseline; it was driven by geopolitical and supply-chain disruption, and it sees 15-20% growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Any lost orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a contract ended and was re-bid on fresh procurement rather than being lost; one Rs 5 crore order was cancelled with re-entry expected in June.

risks_watch: Component price inflation and vendor price validity (30 days) could further pressure margins on new orders and limit bid participation.
Management's 3-4 month normalisation timeline is industry-based and not confirmed; analyst challenged it as possibly optimistic.

Revenue visibility: Rs 20-22 crore of the Rs 32 crore book billable in H1 FY27, and the FY27 growth target relies on pipeline conversion that management could not quantify; DPDP and BFSI order flow are unproven.
Working capital: management acknowledged the government-heavy mix lengthens the working capital cycle.
Management said the Rs 5 crore re-entry is expected in June; watch whether it is re-won.

Full-year numbers reported on a consolidated basis; several figures were stated imprecisely on the call (for example the Rs 100 crore baseline and the 15% vs 15-20% growth references), so reconcile against the filed results.
544471|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on balance sheet and long-term strategy, but cautious and sometimes evasive on forward numbers: management declined point revenue guidance and gave ranges and qualitative targets. It was emphatic that there were no execution failures and that the H2 shortfall was a deliberate choice to avoid loss-making fixed-price contracts.

So, one 5 crore order, we didn't lose it, but we, with the good relation with the customer, we managed to, get it, get the, get it canceled.
Our debt-to-equity ratio is lowest in our peer groups, which stands at just 0.12.

544476|2026-03.headline: Jeena Sikho Q4 FY26 revenue rose 55% YoY to INR216 crore, but PAT fell QoQ to INR45 crore after about INR21 crore of one-time charges.
544476|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue from operations reached INR801 crore (+71%), EBITDA INR349 crore (44% margin, +1,360 bps) and PAT INR222 crore (+177%), with no debt. Q4 revenue was INR216 crore (+55% YoY) and EBITDA INR78 crore (36% margin), but management attributed the sequential profit drop to about INR21 crore of one-time items linked to labour code, ECL provisioning, Ind AS lease accounting and bonuses. Management said the operating base is stable and pointed to new bed capacity, OTC product launches and insurance/Ayushman scheme tie-ups as drivers. Several answers were unquantified or deflected to a later email follow-up.

guidance_outlook: About 2,300 operational beds to reach 2,800-3,000 within 3-4 months; management also said 3,000-3,500 by March 31, 2027.
Target of 7,000-10,000 beds in 3-5 years; revenue target INR3,000 crore in 3-5 years, split roughly 50:50 products and services.

Says Ayushman scheme rates of INR8,800-9,400 per day and insurance rates of INR8,800-9,200 per day could lift revenue per bed; the scheme is expected in 1-2 months but is unconfirmed.
capex_capacity: Operational beds about 2,300, with 445 more in active deployment; management said non-operational beds were deliberately held back during the Iran-America conflict due to cost.
Block additions in FY26 were INR42 crore (INR32 crore new assets, ~INR10 crore from WIP).

Planned facilities: large hospital in Lucknow (finalisation this week), Ahmedabad, new property in Patna, Kolkata property found, new Pune centre, Mumbai bed expansion, Panchkula wellness centre in June, ultra-luxury 108-room Manali centre in July.
Claims it can add 2,000 beds within 9-12 months once government payment portal is fixed; seven UP colleges identified.
Setup cost INR3-4 lakh per bed; claims payback under 6 months for small facilities and 71% three-year average ROCE (company claim).
demand_pricing: FY26 IPD volume +65% to 40,450; OPD volume +69% to over 600,000; Q4 OPD/COD/video consult patients +247% YoY, daycare +139%, IPD +84%.

Management attributed a slight Q4 volume dip to deferred preventive bookings in March amid war-related panic; said about 250 advance-booked patients were affected and Meerut census averaged 316 recently.
Repeat rates for last quarter: 26% for admitted hospital patients and 34% for products (products only about 6 months old).
Management computes revenue of INR4,650 per bed-day on 2,300 beds (INR375 crore over 8.28 lakh bed-days), versus average ticket of INR8,000-8,200 per admitted patient.
Government sales were deliberately cut due to delayed payments and credit provisioning; management said private hospital business is the focus.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 OPD, IPD and daycare volumes decline slightly QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed war-related panic in March, when advance-booked preventive patients deferred visits; said only about 250 bookings were affected and volumes have recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Will product sales growth resume after the Entero tie-up, given Q4 medicine sales of INR118 crore vs INR121 crore in Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Entero model stalled because Entero wanted the company to bear costs, so it shifted to newspaper, social media and TV spend and launched two products in May; impact expected in 2-4 months. INR2-4 crore QoQ swings described as immaterial.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR21 crore one-off is recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said INR19-20 crore is one-time (INR7 crore employee benefits and INR5 crore ECL one-time, plus leasehold and depreciation effects) and about INR2 crore is recurring; leasehold impact to be spread evenly from next year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q4 EBITDA margin about 46% excluding one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed with the analyst's framing and cited FY26 EBITDA of INR349 crore on INR801 crore, about 45%, versus INR125 crore (27%) in FY25.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue mix outlook at INR3,000 crore and will margins stay similar?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the mix will be about 50:50 products and services (48% services, 52% products in the latest period) and that both segments will grow in parallel with similar margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is the bed addition path to 7,000-10,000 beds?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it can add 2,000 beds in 9-12 months once demand and government payment readiness allow; growth may be lumpy and depends on changing public narrative toward preventive care.

risks_watch: Q4 margin is reported after about INR21 crore of items management calls one-time; recurring components (about INR2 crore, plus lease and depreciation changes) need tracking next quarter.
Bed utilisation and volume momentum depend on preventive demand, which slipped in March amid geopolitical headlines; management is betting on 3-4 months to change public perception.
Government business was cut to about INR36 crore from INR118 crore; Ayushman scheme and UP cashless scheme timing is unconfirmed and based on management statements.
Product growth is untested: nine OTC products are under three months old, repeat rates were 34% for products, and several medicine launches were deferred from February.

Auditor transition to Grant Thornton drove accounting changes (advance booking practice, leasehold provisioning, bonuses); the result release was delayed to May 30, 2026, and management did not provide full segment profitability.

Several analyst questions were deflected to a post-call email follow-up; governance and disclosure quality is a watch item, including the earnings call held on June 2, 2026 with the transcript filed June 8.
544476|2026-03.management_tone: Highly confident and promotional, with bold long-range targets (INR3,000 crore revenue, 7,000-10,000 beds) and frequent references to policy tailwinds. Cautious and deflective on Q4 quarter-on-quarter details, often referring analysts to the CFO or to email follow-ups.
key_quotes: Our company is not a wellness company; it is a mainstream healthcare provider, measured just like any other hospital in India.
I just need to admit 140000 people, and my turnover will reach INR1500 crores.
I am telling you again, all the big hospitals in India, whether Allopathy or Ayurveda, will have to remove their dependency on government business.
I clarify that the Q4 earnings decline is solely due to these one-time items and does not reflect any weakness in the business.

544476|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of INR224 crore (up 29% YoY), EBITDA of INR92 crore (up 17% YoY, 41% margin) and PAT of INR65 crore. Management guided to 30% annual growth and INR3,000 crore turnover within about 3 to 5 years, but gave no quantified FY27 guidance beyond 3,000 to 3,500 operational beds.

544491|2026-06.headline: Gem Aromatics Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose to INR83 crore (from INR76 crore) but consolidated EBITDA fell to INR3.3 crore (3.3% margin) and consolidated PAT was a INR7.9 crore loss.

544527|2026-06.headline: Atlanta Electricals Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 48% YoY to INR466.33 crore; record order inflow of INR972.42 crore lifted order book to INR3,116.63 crore.

Order inflow was a record INR972.42 crore, taking the unexecuted order book to about INR3,117 crore, of which about INR2,400 crore is expected to execute in FY27. Management reiterated a 40% revenue CAGR target and a 17-18% margin range, while 400 kV and 765 kV product timelines were pushed out and largely remain conditional.

MTF book reached ₹13,318 million (+55% YoY) and distribution AUM ₹94,791 million (+25.82% YoY). Management guided MTF to ₹1,750–1,800 crores and distribution AUM up 40% by year-end FY27.

Distribution AUM targeted to grow about 40%, driven by higher wallet share of existing clients.
Continue to target a near 50:50 broking to non-broking income mix over the medium term.
Long-term revenue growth band of 15–25% (typically 20–25%); PAT growth target of around 30–35% while the mix is not yet 50:50.

Management said borrowing is being used to fund working capital and MTF; it expects leverage to rise from 0.81x.
Credit rating upgraded: short-term bank facilities to A1+, long-term to A+.
Dubai subsidiary planned for NRI servicing; a GIFT City subsidiary already exists and is active for NRI business.

RBI revised capital market exposure framework effective 1 July 2026 is expected to raise bank working-capital costs for broking intermediaries.
MTF yield about 14%; management said spreads depend on market liquidity and borrowing costs, which are currently higher.
Demat accounts reached 23 crore in June; SIP additions about 66 lakh in June versus 53 lakh in March; 42 companies filed draft offer documents with SEBI in the quarter.

Distribution revenue in April–June fell QoQ because insurance sales are concentrated in January–March; mutual fund and other AUM grew QoQ and the company recorded its highest net collections in the last quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why was MTF interest income flat despite about 21% book growth, and is MTF pricing falling?
qa_highlights.answer: Average MTF book was flat QoQ because it fell to about ₹1,100 crores in March after a mid-cap sell-off of about 15%, then recovered to ₹1,330 crores by quarter end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MTF risk management approach?
qa_highlights.answer: MTF is funded only against cash-market securities chosen from a restricted list, with no F&O allocation, per-customer and per-scrip limits, and a book mostly below ₹1 crore per client. Management said there have been no delinquencies since 2017.

qa_highlights.question: What was the fraud, and what has been done to prevent recurrence?
qa_highlights.answer: Two dormant depository clients lost securities through fraudulent off-market transfers noticed about a year later. The company replenished the securities, filed an FIR with EOW (assets frozen), lodged an insurance claim, appointed EY for forensic audit and hired an external consultant. Recoveries will be booked only when reasonably certain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue growth guidance given the 22% Q1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it aims for 20–25% growth, within a 15–25% range, with PAT growth of 30–35%, until the 50:50 broking and non-broking mix is reached.

qa_highlights.question: Why did non-broking decline QoQ and how will this be avoided?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said distribution is seasonal, with insurance sales concentrated in January–March; the April–June fall was driven by insurance, while other products grew. Trail revenue was also hit by the March market fall.

qa_highlights.question: Why is debt-equity elevated and will leverage increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt-equity fell after the IPO equity infusion; management intends to borrow more to fund MTF and working capital, saying 1.5–2x is comfortable for the industry, versus 0.81x now.

qa_highlights.question: What is the MTF yield and the sustainability of spreads?
qa_highlights.answer: MTF yield is about 14%. Management said spreads depend on liquidity, with borrowing costs currently higher, and that higher costs can be passed to clients.

risks_watch: ₹209.96 million exceptional fraud charge; recovery depends on insurance claim settlement and frozen assets, with timing uncertain. External forensic audit still in progress.
RBI capital market exposure framework from 1 July 2026 may raise bank borrowing costs and working-capital needs for brokers.
MTF book (₹13,318 million) is sensitive to market sell-offs, as the March 2026 trough showed; leverage is planned to rise from 0.81x.
Derivatives activity is moderating under SEBI curbs, and distribution revenue is seasonal.
Dubai subsidiary licensing and GIFT City international offering are still early-stage.

544546|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue rose 42.5% to INR84.22 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to 17% and PAT margin to 10.9% as spending on talent, platform and new verticals rose.
544546|2026-03.overview: Chatterbox Technologies held its maiden earnings call for FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026), its first since its IPO. Revenue from operations grew 42.5% YoY to INR84.22 crores, and EBITDA and PAT rose in absolute terms to INR14.32 crores and INR9.2 crores. Margins moderated, which management attributed to investment in talent, platform capabilities and new verticals. Management declined to give formal guidance, though it said FY27 net margins would be similar to FY26 with an aim to expand them. Several questions focused on the sharp fall in market cap after listing, the possibility of a QYOU Media merger, the delayed results timeline, and the AAGE edutainment app; management answered most of these qualitatively or deferred them.

segments.commentary: Contributed 24.55% of FY26 revenue. Management called it one of the fastest-growing verticals and among the highest-margin, and said it expects revenue to at least double in the coming period, without giving a percentage target.

segments.name: International (Chtr International / Dubai subsidiary)
segments.commentary: About 18% of FY26 revenue. Dubai subsidiary is the gateway to the Middle East; priority markets are MENA, with APAC and LATAM evaluated selectively. Management said it will expand in a lean way.

guidance_outlook: No formal financial guidance given. Management said the opportunity ahead is significantly larger and it remains optimistic on healthy medium- to long-term growth.

ChtrSocial expected to at least double its revenue in the upcoming period; no percentage target given.
AAGE edutainment app launch targeted within FY27 after development was paused for the IPO; it is still at the UX/UI stage with focus-group validation planned.
Management said integrated benefits from QYOU Media collaboration will become more visible in H2 2026.
capex_capacity: Intangible assets roughly doubled, while intangible assets under development stayed at INR4.68 crores; the AAGE app was on hold during the IPO and is being resumed.

No capacity, utilisation or capex figures were disclosed.
demand_pricing: Management said growth came from a mix of higher ticket sizes, organic growth across verticals, new client wins and international expansion, with an equal-mix view endorsed by the analyst.

Management does not disclose net revenue retention, but said a significant part of growth came from existing enterprise clients with larger mandates and cross-selling of ChtrSocial and Studios.

Consolidated net worth rose from INR86 crore to INR194 crore after the IPO, while working capital increased on higher volumes and overseas inventory. Management declined to give FY27 revenue guidance, citing the Middle East conflict, and reiterated a medium-term target of INR600-700 crore revenue in 2.5-3 years.

544600|2026-03.headline: Lenskart Q4 FY26 revenue rose 41% YoY to ₹2,516 crore, with reported EBITDA up 61% and pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin at 12.8%.
544600|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was the strongest quarter since listing: revenue grew 41% YoY to ₹2,516 crore, PAT reached ₹204 crore, and EBITDA margin expanded 2.7 pp to 21.3%. India and international both grew, with India same-store sales growth at 24% and international revenue up 35.4%. FY26 crossed ₹1,700 crore EBITDA, ₹1,000 crore pre-Ind AS EBITDA and ₹500 crore PAT for the first time. Management kept the steady-state pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin at about 25% and guided FY27 net store additions to roughly FY26 levels (542 in India plus 61 international in FY26).

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,054 crore (+35.4% YoY; +25% constant currency) with eyewear units up 29%. Store count 718 after 13 net adds in Q4 and 61 in FY26; FY26 pre-Ind AS EBITDA ₹264 crore at 7% margin. Japan was the strongest market; Middle East had a temporary traffic dip that has recovered to near normal.

guidance_outlook: Net new store additions in FY27 expected to be around FY26 levels (FY26: 542 India, 61 international).
Long-term steady-state pre-Ind AS EBITDA margin unchanged at approximately 25% (India currently 14-15%, about 10 pp runway).
Quarterly margins will vary with store-opening phasing, seasonality and long-term bets; management said it will prioritise long-term value over short-term linearity.
Management urged investors to track trailing 12-month volume growth as the cleanest measure of underlying demand.
Step-up in R&D spend in FY27 for automated eye testing, smart eyewear (B by Lenskart) and AI; FY27 priorities include scaling to 100 million customers.
capex_capacity: FY26 store capex funded 603 net new stores (ops cash flow ₹887 crore), alongside manufacturing investment including the new Hyderabad facility.
Factory floors to move toward near full automation from the current 75%; Bhiwadi centralised facility supports next-day delivery across 78 cities (from 7 cities initially, about 30 later).
Hyderabad plant and Thailand JV cited as structural answers to reduce import dependence.
Remote optometry stores rose 3.7x in a year to 623.
India eyewear units reached 29 million in FY26 (18 million two years earlier); long-term store runway of 4,500 stores in India previously articulated, management said more is possible.
demand_pricing: India same-store sales growth 24% in Q4 (broad-based across Metro, Tier 1, Tier 2); same-pincode sales growth 31%. Management declined to split SSSG into value and volume; it rejected an analyst's estimate of ~10% volume SSS as too low.
Eye tests: 6.8 million globally in Q4 (+45% YoY); India eye tests 6 million (+50%); about half of India eye tests were first-time exams. Gold active members 8.8 million (+29.5%).
Product margin in India held at 64% despite rupee depreciation; management said structural margin gains were offset by currency (RMB 11 to 14 cited as an example).
ASP fluctuations are driven by OPP campaigns (New Lens Replacement, Hustlr) and by upgrades to Own days, Meller, progressives.
International ACP reduction ongoing as markets are integrated into central supply chain; operating leverage seen after scale in Singapore, Dubai and now Japan.
Meller sunglasses out of stock in all markets; launched in 1,000+ India stores, Middle East and Southeast Asia, with Japan next.

qa_highlights.question: What geopolitical, raw material, China-sourcing or market risks should investors monitor?
qa_highlights.answer: Freight and raw material have had no meaningful impact so far; currency is the biggest variable. 42% of business is international and vertical integration has offset rupee-import headwinds. No material demand impact seen in India or abroad; Middle East dip was small and brief.

qa_highlights.question: How was the India gross margin held near 64% in a low-ASP quarter, and does SSSG of ~25% with ~15% price imply ~10% volume growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin gains came from vertical integration and process changes, not price increases; OPP campaigns are paired with upgrades to offset margin. Management said the 10% volume estimate was not correct and that volume SSS is meaningfully higher; it does not disclose value/volume split.

qa_highlights.question: How will employee productivity and cost leverage trend, especially internationally?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating leverage came mainly from SSG and volume growth on a fixed cost base. HQ and tech costs were flat as headcount was not added; AI and remote optometry are expected to add more output per person.

qa_highlights.question: Does Tier 2 strength expand the 4,500-store runway and allow faster expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said more than 4,500 stores are possible; 200+ Tier 2 stores have been added and feed GeoIQ. Metros are also growing (eye tests +45%+) and are the main source of SSG.

qa_highlights.question: How should we think about competition in smart glasses (e.g. Google re-entry)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the category is very early with no clear form-factor winner; it sees Lenskart's role in prescription and distribution of smart glasses and its app/data layer as advantages. Launch focus is on learning, not near-term sales.

qa_highlights.question: How will international margins converge to India's level, and what is the KSA breakeven status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a quarter for reaching 15% international margin; it cited falling ACP and operating leverage after scale. KSA is about two years old and ahead of where UAE was at the same stage; no breakeven date was given.

qa_highlights.answer: Site selection is bottom-up using mobility data within a 10-minute travel radius, not pincode-level. Management said stores tripled in many cities while revenue doubled, and that much of SSG came from multi-store pincodes.

qa_highlights.question: Is same-day delivery a near-term target and does the store network become an inventory model?

544600|2026-06.headline: Lenskart Q1 FY27 revenue grew 34% YoY and PAT rose 182% to ₹228 crore, with India same-store sales growth at 18.3%.

qa_highlights.question: Will store expansion from ~2,700 to ~10,000 stores hurt same-store sales?
