544657|2026-03.headline: FY26 total income rose 37.19% to INR256.92 crore, but EBITDA margin compressed to about 11% in H2 on forex and RCN prices; management guides 15-16%.
544657|2026-03.overview: Pajson Agro's first earnings call after its December listing covered FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026). Total income grew 37.19% YoY to INR256.92 crore, EBITDA grew 24.98% and PAT grew 21.4%, with the company maintaining a double-digit full-year EBITDA margin. H2 saw margin compression from a spike in raw cashew nut (RCN) prices, forex movement (rupee moved about 10.5% from April 2025 base) and shipping disruptions, with H2 total income up 37.38% to INR138.5 crore and H2 PAT up 8.97%. Capacity utilisation was 86% on an 18,000 MT Andhra Pradesh plant, and a greenfield 35,000 MT Vizianagaram facility (targeting 70,000 MT total by FY30) is being built with INR39.53 crore of POs committed by March 2026.

financial_highlights.value: Double-digit full-year EBITDA margin (exact value not stated)

financial_highlights.metric: Average realisation per kg RCN processed

segments.name: Institutional B2B (cashew kernels)
segments.commentary: Serves large confectionery and snack manufacturers as the high-volume base; about 78% of repeat revenue comes from existing customers, per management. Customer visibility is only 1 to 3 months, and new capacity has no committed orders yet.

segments.name: Distribution / Royal Mewa brand (dry fruits)
segments.commentary: Brand revenue grew about 6.5x in FY26; distribution network covers over 170 distributors across 20+ states. Online presence on Amazon and Jio; quick-commerce listings (Blinkit, Zepto) in process.

guidance_outlook: Steady-state EBITDA margin guided at 15% to 16% for FY27, with management saying it expects a couple of percentage points of improvement in FY28 from scale; no exact number given.
Existing 18,000 MT capacity expected to grow revenue about 20% in FY27 (about 20% to 22% from current levels per different answers).
New Vizianagaram plant: trial production November or December 2026 (FY27), commercial production from Q4 FY27; utilisation about 15% in FY27, 65-70% in FY28, 85-90% the year after.
Peak revenue potential from new capacity about INR475 crore at 85% utilisation; management also said revenue at 70% utilisation for FY28 would be lower.
Debt-to-equity currently about 0.25, which management wants to stay within; working capital to be funded mainly by internal accruals, supplier credit and some borrowing growth.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity: 8,500 MT (FY23), 12,000 MT (FY24 and FY25), 18,000 MT (FY26). FY26 utilisation 86%.

Total capex for the new capacity about INR76 crore excluding land (land acquired in FY25). IPO proceeds of about INR74.45 crore: INR57 crore for the new facility, INR10.42 crore for general corporate purposes.
POs issued to vendors as of 31 March 2026 about INR39.5 crore, with advances of about INR10.5 crore paid; further POs of INR20-25 crore planned in Q1 FY27.
Machinery sourcing: some from Vietnam, some from China, about 40-45% indigenous from India. Greenfield line capacity of 100 tons per line, with automation targeted.
Plan to reach 70,000 MT capacity by FY30 with a near-zero-waste ecosystem.
demand_pricing: Average RCN realisation about INR161.5/kg in FY26 vs about INR160/kg in FY25; kernel realisation about INR660/kg; average kernel yield 24.57%.
Wholes-to-pieces recovery mix about 70:30.

Raw material sourcing: about 93-94% imported from West Africa (Cote d'Ivoire, Guinea-Bissau and others) and 6-8% domestic Indian crop in the last year; about 60% sourced from Cote d'Ivoire and Guinea-Bissau per Chairman.
Management said India consumes 2.0-2.2 million tons of RCN vs 400-500 thousand tons domestic production, so Indian prices track West African prices.

Margin pressure came from forex (rupee moved about 10.5%), RCN price spikes in H2, IPO expenses charged to P&L and shipping costs; management says part of the cost is being passed to customers via price increases and part to suppliers.
No exports in FY26 (some cargoes in FY25); export plans tied to new plant.

qa_highlights.question: How much of new capacity is backed by customer orders?
qa_highlights.answer: No firm orders yet; institutional visibility is only 1-3 months. Repeat revenue is about 78% from existing customers, and management says it is unable to serve all new demand.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables and inventory rise?
qa_highlights.answer: FY25 plant was shut for expansion and stock was sold off. FY26 focused on institutional customers, which carry more credit. Inventory about INR38 crore and debtors about INR18 crore; creditors rose to about INR20 crore from INR3 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of West Asia crisis and forex on margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said shipments come directly from Africa to India, so no supply disruption. Forex (procurement side, since raw material is imported) drove the margin dip; hedging via banks is being initiated and shipping lines approached for longer-term contracts.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 15-16% EBITDA for FY27 and a couple of percentage points improvement in FY28 from scale.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the new facility and deployment of IPO funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction on schedule and structure ordered; POs of about INR39.5 crore issued by March, advances of about INR10.5 crore, and INR20-25 crore more POs in Q1 FY27. Trial production targeted November or December 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Short-term borrowing and cost?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR20 crore short-term working capital from bankers; the rate was about 8.4% last year and management said it has come down about 25 bps this year. Short-term loans and advances of INR31.95 crore were advances to suppliers in February.

risks_watch: Forex: rupee depreciation raises import cost for RCN; hedging policies not yet fully in place.
Shipping and fuel costs linked to Middle East disruption, though management says West African routes are unaffected.
Customer visibility is only 1-3 months and new capacity has no committed orders; ramp-up to 85-90% utilisation depends on demand.
Rising trade receivables and inventory (working capital intensity) as institutional sales expand on credit.
Execution risk on the Vizianagaram plant: trial production Nov-Dec 2026, commercial Q4 FY27, and remaining capex and POs of about INR20-25 crore in Q1 FY27.
Royal Mewa brand growth may require higher advertising spend, which management says will be kept within the 15-16% margin band.
Management's answers on the new capacity's revenue and margin profile were not consistent across the call (for example, 20% vs 20-22% growth and the INR475 crore peak revenue figure).
544657|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, capacity and the brand, but cautious on margins, which were guided down to 15-16% and attributed mainly to forex and RCN price swings. Answers on new-plant revenue and margin differentiation were sometimes vague or inconsistent, and some numbers were corrected or restated during the Q&A.
key_quotes: We are operating in a perform or perish era and Pajson is firmly in the perform category.
So we expect the margins to be steady.
We have the capacity, we have the brand, and now we have the capital.

544658|2026-06.headline: ICICI Pru AMC Q1 FY27 PAT rose 23.1% YoY to INR965 crore on 18.3% YoY MF AUM growth and a mark-to-market gain in other income.
544658|2026-06.overview: Quarter-average mutual fund AUM reached INR11.17 lakh crore, up 1.1% QoQ and 18.3% YoY, with market share of 13.4% and second-place ranking. Operating revenue rose 17.6% YoY to INR1,564 crore, and other income swung to INR181 crore positive on June-end mark-to-market gains. Operating expenses rose 14.3% QoQ, mainly from employee costs, with ESOP charges now debited for the first time. Operating PBT was INR1,100 crore (+20.2% YoY) and PAT INR965 crore (+23.1% YoY). Industry SIP flows were flat-to-soft in the quarter and June rebounded, while the company said its own numbers track the industry.

financial_highlights.change: Positive vs negative in previous quarter, on mark-to-market

segments.name: Mutual fund
segments.commentary: Share of operating net revenue 90.02%; market share 13.4% overall, 13.5% in active schemes (INR9.25 lakh crore), 14% in equity (INR6.31 lakh crore). Equity-oriented hybrid QAAUM INR2.22 lakh crore, 26.6% share.

segments.name: Alternates (PMS, AIF, private credit, real estate, PE, offshore advisory)
segments.commentary: QAAUM INR79,446 crore; PMS INR28,996 crore (+8.1% QoQ); AIF INR22,737 crore. Share of operating net revenue 8.54%.

segments.name: Advisory
segments.commentary: Share of operating net revenue 1.44%; yield on assets under advisory 30 bps. AUM moderated on international redemptions, per management.

segments.name: SIF (iSIF)
segments.commentary: QAAUM INR2,678 crore; four of seven permitted strategies launched, two of them in June 2026.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal guidance; it pointed to the June-quarter employee cost as the run-rate base.
ESOP cost for FY27 indicated at INR64-68 crore, charged evenly across quarters.
No negative impact from TER regulation changes; the company said it passed the change through to distributors.
Management said several product launches are planned over the next nine months, including life-cycle funds, a contra fund, ETFs, a SIF sector rotation strategy and commercial real estate AIFs.
capex_capacity: Presence in more than 300 towns; new office openings are decided at regional level each year.
Four iSIF strategies live and three permitted strategies still pending, with one more approval in hand (sector rotation SIF).
GIFT City: one inbound fund (ICICI Prudential Smart Navigator Fund) live; more inbound and outbound products under evaluation.
Investment book: about 50% is seed capital, largely marked to market under the SEBI formula; the AIF/other equity/REIT share of the investment book is 23.5% and its MTM exposure was not disclosed.
demand_pricing: Industry QAAUM INR83.28 lakh crore, +15.4% YoY and +2% QoQ; closing AUM +11.6% QoQ. Equity AUM INR45.2 lakh crore.
Industry equity net flows INR1.14 lakh crore, down INR10,064 crore QoQ; June flows rebounded 26% MoM. June SIP contribution INR31,781 crore, roughly flat QoQ.
Company systematic transactions (SIP plus STP) were INR4,872 crore in June vs INR5,104 crore in March 2026.
Debt QAAUM down 6% QoQ to INR11.93 lakh crore on institutional redemptions amid tight corporate liquidity.
Equity distribution mix: MFDs 36.2%, national distributors 15.9%, ICICI Bank 7.7%, other banks 10.7%, direct 29.5%.
Margins (annualised): equity 66 bps, debt 32 bps, liquid 12 bps, passive 12 bps, arbitrage 30 bps. Alternates net yield 95 bps, which management said normally runs 90-100 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 23% PAT growth and what helped in Q1 despite geopolitics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited resilient industry net flows and SIP over the prior year. Net sales were over INR4.6 lakh crore in FY26, and mark-to-market gains on the equity base also lifted PAT.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the change in market share, flows vs MTM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said quarterly share shifts are mainly MTM-driven given the high equity AUM base. Small caps returned 24%, mid caps 17.2% and large caps 8.9%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ESOP cost and how should employee opex be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 ESOP cost is INR64-68 crore, charged evenly (not front-loaded). Management said the June quarter's INR200 crore quarterly opex is a fair base for modelling.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SIP flows fall and what is the ticket-size or stoppage picture?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the net SIP trigger fell because stoppages of older SIPs exceeded new SIP registrations. It said count does not matter and only the net effect is shown. It did not split SIP by ticket size or scheme.

qa_highlights.question: Why did debt AUM fall in the quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to institutional redemptions as corporates used liquidity for working capital during the war-related disruption, not to seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for alternates net yield and new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Net yield typically runs 90-100 bps depending on product mix. Life-cycle MF funds follow SEBI's predefined expense structure and start equity-heavy, then shift to debt nearer maturity.

qa_highlights.question: Is staff cost going to moderate after Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is the run rate. Compensation changes take effect from 1 April, with employee costs up 11% YoY. QoQ growth was partly due to reversals in Q4 FY26 and to campus hiring in Q1.

risks_watch: SIP trigger and June SIP run-rate (INR31,781 crore industry; company SIP+STP INR4,872 crore in June) as the next test of retail flow stickiness.
Debt AUM outflows from institutional and corporate liquidity; mix of debt AUM is a watch item.
MTM sensitivity: about 50% of the investment book is seed capital, so the other income line swings with markets (INR181 crore this quarter vs negative in Q4 FY26).
Alternates yield and mix shifts; PMS/AIF net yield of 95 bps with fees and commissions rising in line with volumes.
Employee costs and ESOP run-rate are now in the P&L; opex growth could stay elevated versus prior-year levels.
SIF category is early-stage; management said distribution is still limited and advisor participation needs to grow.
544658|2026-06.management_tone: Confident on the franchise and long-term flows, but guarded on near-term SIP and debt trends, which management repeatedly said should be read quarterly rather than monthly. Management was evasive on the SIP ticket-size breakdown, the MTM share of alternates and the 23.5% investment-book split, and gave no formal guidance.
key_quotes: So, the change in our market share has also been predominantly on account of mark-to-market.
Frankly the count wise it does not matter. No one should look at from a count perspective.
it is a moderate return world and the series of products that we have created on dynamic asset allocation.
So whether it is private equity, whether it is any of the alternate products, you won't see the entire sales been reflected in the numbers per se.

544658|2026-09.headline: ICICI Pru AMC Q2 FY27 operating revenue rose 16.3% YoY to INR1,674 crore, but PAT fell 7.8% QoQ to INR889 crore on lower other income.
544658|2026-09.overview: Operating revenue grew 16.3% YoY and 7% QoQ to INR1,674 crore, and operating PBT rose 15.7% YoY to INR1,181 crore. PAT of INR889 crore was up 6.1% YoY but down 7.8% QoQ, mainly because other income of INR16.9 crore fell on mark-to-market. Total mutual fund QAAUM reached INR11.61 lakh crore (+14.4% YoY), with equity QAAUM at INR6.59 lakh crore (+16.3% YoY) and 13.7% market share. Management said industry gross flows were steady and the net flow decline came from higher redemptions, and it declared an interim dividend of INR30 per share.

financial_highlights.metric: Gross / net yield (H1 FY27, annualised, company level)

segments.name: Mutual fund
segments.commentary: Total QAAUM INR11.61 lakh crore (+14.4% YoY), 13.3% market share, second-largest AMC. Equity QAAUM INR6.59 lakh crore with 13.7% share; equity-oriented hybrid QAAUM INR2.29 lakh crore with 26.4% share.

segments.name: Alternates
segments.commentary: QAAUM INR80,965 crore. PMS QAAUM INR30,791 crore (+21.4% YoY); AIF QAAUM INR24,260 crore. H1 FY27 PMS and AIF gross yield 1.92%, net yield 0.96%.

segments.name: Advisory
segments.commentary: Assets under advisory yield 0.32% in H1 FY27. Management said advisory AUM, mostly international money, has seen outflows for about 1.5 years.

segments.name: SIF
segments.commentary: QAAUM INR4,948 crore in Q2 FY27 versus INR2,678 crore in Q1 FY27. Four strategies are live; a fifth fund was to launch in the quarter.

guidance_outlook: Full-year ESOP cost guided at INR64-68 crore, charged pro rata to P&L.
Alternates net yield broadly expected in the INR90-95 bps range (management also cited 90-100 bps); no yield guidance for mutual funds.
Opex growth in H1 FY27 described as in line with normal increase; no segment-wise opex split given.
PMS business acquisition from ICICI Securities (about INR3,000 crore AUM) pending regulatory approvals.
No infrastructure fund planned; focus on scaling private credit, real estate (pre-leased office), private equity and early-stage PE.
capex_capacity: PMS business acquisition from ICICI Securities approved by the board; approvals and documentation in progress.
Launched in Q2: Balanced Hybrid Fund, Multi Asset Active FoF, Dynamic Asset Allocation Passive FoF, BSE Insurance ETF and three Life Cycle Funds (2031, 2036, 2041 maturities).
Debt AIF strategy not yet launched; management will explore it at an appropriate time.
Structures set up in GIFT City, Luxembourg and Southeast Asia for international advisory funds.
demand_pricing: Industry QAAUM INR87.49 lakh crore (+13.4% YoY, +5.1% QoQ); industry equity QAAUM INR48.19 lakh crore (+15.3% YoY).
Industry equity net flows INR1.06 lakh crore in Q2, down about 7% QoQ; mid and small caps took 36% of H1 FY27 net equity sales versus 22% in FY26.
Company equity distribution mix: MFD 36.1%, national distributors 15.9%, ICICI Bank 7.5%, other banks 10.6%, direct 29.9%.

Management said industry gross flows were steady; the net flow decline was driven by higher redemptions, particularly in BAF and MAF hybrid funds. Monthly SIPs stable; September SIP at INR32,490 crore industry-wide.
Company systematic transactions (SIP plus STP) moderated to INR4,672 crore in September from INR4,872 crore in June.

qa_highlights.question: Why has ICICI Bank channel AUM not grown while other channels grew?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ICICI Bank is an important channel that it works on equally with all others; the outcome depends on each distributor's strategy. The company's ICICI Bank share of the channel was described as about the same as before.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving the flow market-share pressure at large AMCs?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross flows were consistent industry-wide, so the net decline was redemption-driven, and redemptions are linked to AUM rather than gross sales. Redemptions are slightly higher, and money moves between schemes and outside the AMC in ways that cannot be tracked.

qa_highlights.question: Why are mutual fund revenue yields rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yield is an outcome of flow mix, including which schemes gain money, old versus new money, and distribution commission, and it does not target a yield.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategy toward mid and small caps?
qa_highlights.answer: Small-cap fund is fully open; mid-cap is being opened slowly. Management prefers large caps now and said it will build mid/small-cap positioning over 5 to 7 years, waiting for valuations to correct.

qa_highlights.question: Are SIF investors existing customers, and what are SIF unit economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management treats SIF as part of mutual funds with a INR10 lakh minimum ticket, and says margins are similar to mutual funds. It uses derivatives defensively and does not allow shorting; the customer mix was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Is the AUM for alternates fee-bearing?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said reported alternates AUM is fee-bearing (drawn-down) AUM only, since fees start on drawdown; committed but undrawn capital is excluded.

risks_watch: Redemptions elevated amid volatile markets; net flows and market share under pressure.
Other income volatility from mark-to-market, which drove the QoQ PAT decline.
SIP composition shifting toward small and mid caps and STP front-loading affecting SIP and lump-sum mix.
Alternates yield at 90-95 bps net; real estate drawdowns and mix changes may move it.
Advisory AUM outflows for about 1.5 years, dependent on international flows.
PMS acquisition from ICICI Securities pending regulatory approvals.
544658|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on franchise, flows and alternates growth, but guarded on near-term outlook, flows and yields, which management repeatedly said depend on market direction. It was evasive on channel-level SIP, ICICI Bank channel and yield questions, and dismissive of an analyst's other-income focus.
key_quotes: It is very clearly understood that equity markets and mutual funds are for the long term.
Redemption is related to the AUM that you have.
We do not give guidance on what we expect of the yield. It's actually an outcome.
So, it is a very simple industry. I think SEBI has created a very simple industry.

544664|2026-03.headline: KSH International Q4 FY26 revenue rose 101% YoY to INR 1,018 crore and EBITDA per ton reached about INR 74,000, with FY26 PAT at a record INR 110 crore.
544664|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 was a strong quarter: revenue from operations of INR 1,018 crore (up 101% YoY), EBITDA of INR 56 crore (from INR 35 crore), and a record quarterly PAT of INR 34.5 crore (up 87%). Volumes were about 7,600 metric tons, up 29% YoY, though Middle East shipments of roughly 100-150 tons slipped from March into April. Management said FY26 EBITDA per ton was about INR 67,600 and guided sustainable EBITDA per ton to a 65,000-74,000 range, with the Supa Phase II expansion (to about 59,000 MT) on track for FY27. Working capital days remain high at 65-68, and management is negotiating bank terms to push payable days above 25-30.

segments.name: Specialized winding wires (incl. CTC)
segments.commentary: About 75% of revenue in FY26 and FY25; grew 62% in FY26 and 103% YoY in Q4. CTC is the majority of specialized wires; management does not disclose CTC volumes. Specialized EBITDA per ton is about 3x standard wires.

segments.name: Standard winding wires
segments.commentary: Grew 58% in FY26 and 80% in Q4 YoY. Management is targeting EVs, AC compressors and motors. About 35% of the 43,445 MT installed capacity is standard.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Q4 export revenue grew 92% YoY (after 37% in Q3 and 22% in Q2). Exports were about 27% of revenue in Q4 (excluding other operating revenue) and all go to T&D customers in four continents.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth expected to be at least the FY26 rate of 21%, as full-year Supa capacity is available.
Sustainable EBITDA per ton range of about 65,000-74,000 (earlier commentary: 67,000-74,000); actual depends on product mix and export share.
Next tranche of new capacity (Supa) expected to come online around Q2 FY27; Supa completion on track for FY27, taking installed capacity to about 59,000 MT.
Green copper backward integration facility expected to commence in H2 FY27.
Payable days targeted above 25 days and close to 30 days by end FY27; working capital days expected to trend lower over the next several quarters.
Operating leverage from new capacity expected to kick in gradually after Q4 FY27; fixed costs of new capacity will persist through FY27.
PEEK insulated wire capacity expected online around end of Q2 FY27; meaningful contribution 1.5-2 years out.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity at March 31, 2026 was 43,445 MT; Supa Phase II expansion takes it to about 59,000 MT, with completion targeted for FY27.
Consolidated utilization was about 70% in Q4 FY26; peak utilization is planned at about 85% of installed capacity, which takes 2-3 years to reach for a new plant.
Around 65% of current installed capacity is for specialized wires and the balance for standard wires.
Space exists for another 10,000 MT at the Supa site (land, building and some utilities already in place); no decision yet.
3.2 MW rooftop solar commissioned at Supa in May 2026, taking total solar capacity to 4 MW for captive use.
Supa began contributing in Q3 FY26 (October 1 onwards) at about 50-55% utilization in the first quarter; Q4 utilization rose further.
demand_pricing: Repeat revenue above 95% in FY26 from more than 120 domestic and global OEM customers; the business is make-to-order with copper and FX passed through.
Some large transformer clients are exploring multi-year supply agreements; management is evaluating the strategic and financial implications.
Middle East impact was limited: some Gulf shipments were delayed by a few weeks and rerouted. Management estimated 200-300 tons of volume effect in Q4 including orders not started.
Management sees no demand deferment from domestic OEMs and no demand reduction from copper prices or the war; freight costs rose but were passed on on CIF basis.

India CTC demand estimated at 100,000-120,000 tons by 2030 versus about 40,000 tons in FY25 and 70,000-75,000 tons expected in FY27-28. Imports were about 1,000 tons a month earlier and are expected to decline.
New entrants could take 5-7 years to qualify for 765 kV/HVDC CTC, according to management.
Pricing is set via one-year or multi-year value-addition matrices agreed with OEMs, not linked to copper price.

qa_highlights.question: Quantify the Middle East impact on Q4.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 100-150 tons of dispatches slipped from March to April. Later, the estimated total effect including orders not started was 200-300 tons.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable EBITDA per ton for FY27-28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 65,000-70,000 per ton is sustainable long term, and later gave 67,000-74,000 as the range.

qa_highlights.question: Will payable days hold, and what is the working capital cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Payable days are targeted above 25 days, and inventory days rose because large transformer orders need full manufacture before dispatch.

qa_highlights.question: How does EBITDA per ton differ between specialized and standard wires?
qa_highlights.answer: Specialized EBITDA per ton is about 3x standard. The blended mix is expected to continue, with both segments growing.

qa_highlights.question: What share of exports and what drives the export growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports are about 30% of revenue, down from a high near 40%, and the target is to return to about 40% over the next couple of years. All exports go to T&D transformer OEMs.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a plan for capacity beyond 59,000 MT?
qa_highlights.answer: Space exists for another 10,000 MT at Supa, with no decision yet. Management would not rule out adding capacity over 24 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any sign of demand deferment from domestic OEMs?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The customer base is diversified and management said it can redirect volumes to other customers.

qa_highlights.question: Will transformer makers backward integrate into CTC?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not see a general trend toward backward integration, given available capacity and the process complexity.

risks_watch: Working capital days stuck at 65-68 and operating cash flow negative in FY26 as receivables and inventory grew; payable-day gains depend on bank negotiations.
Middle East shipment timing and transport cost inflation, which can delay quarterly volumes.
Copper price moves distort reported margins even though EBITDA per ton is less affected.
EBITDA per ton could fall if standard wires grow faster than specialized wires, diluting the mix.
Supa Phase II timing (Q2 FY27 onward) and the ramp-up to 85% utilization taking 2-3 years.
New CTC entrants and imports, although management expects qualification to take 5-7 years.

key_quotes: Specialized wire revenues overall also grew 103% YoY compared to 50 -60% growth in the prior two quarters.
So we expect that at least for FY27 our fixed cost will play out for the new capacity as it has played out in the last two quarters.
Now during Q4 FY26, we reported a quarterly record PAT of INR 34.5 crore, which increased 87% from Q4 of FY25.
This quarter, coppe r prices increased sharply, negatively impacting margins, but as you can see, did not impact EBITDA per ton.

financial_highlights.change: from about INR 64,500 in Q3 and INR 60,000 a year ago

544664|2026-06.headline: KSH International Q1 FY27 revenue rose 108% YoY to INR1,164 crore; EBITDA per ton hit ~INR93,000, with management guiding to a sustainable ~INR75,000.
544664|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR1,164 crore (+108% YoY) and EBITDA was INR74.4 crore (vs INR40.3 crore a year ago and INR56.3 crore in Q4), with a record quarterly PAT of INR42.2 crore. Management attributed the strong EBITDA per ton mainly to a record CTC contribution, higher exports and new OEM customers priced at market-linked value-addition rates, with a weaker rupee also helping. Phase 1 of the Supa expansion is complete, with 14,400 MT of the 30,000 MT phase 2 added so far and full 59,000 MT installed capacity targeted by March 2027. Management signed a five-year framework agreement with Hitachi Energy, though quantity and price are not yet defined.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR40.3 crore YoY; vs INR56.3 crore QoQ
+86% YoY; +22% vs INR34.5 crore in Q4

financial_highlights.metric: Export share of operating revenue (ex other operating revenue)
financial_highlights.change: vs ~29% in Q1 FY26 (as cited by analyst)
+30% YoY vs 6,100 MT; +5% QoQ vs ~7,600 MT
vs 65 days in Q4; vs 71 days a year ago

544679|2026-03.headline: Amagi FY26 revenue rose 30% to INR 1,506 crores and turned PAT positive at INR 72 crores, swinging about INR 140 crores from a FY25 loss.

544679|2026-06.overview: This transcript is of an educational investor webinar titled "AI in Media", hosted by Amagi on July 7, 2026 and filed under Regulation 30, not an earnings call. The moderator stated upfront that company financial performance, outlook and operational metrics would not be addressed. The CEO Baskar Subramanian framed AI as reshaping the video value chain across production, preparation (metadata, encoding, scheduling), distribution (agent-to-agent deals) and consumer discovery. He cited a claim that every $1 spent on technology brings $2 to $4 of human toil, and said most customers view AI as expansionary rather than a cost-saving tool today. No Q1 FY27 results, segment data or guidance were given.
guidance_outlook: No company guidance given; the moderator stated financial performance, business outlook and operational metrics would not be addressed.
Management described AI-driven production cost deflation as a multi-year shift, saying the next few years would bring a fundamental change, without quantifying it.
Management said outcome-based pricing is early and not yet visible in media, and that the core system is expected to stay as is while expansion revenue is driven by outcomes.
capex_capacity: Management said AI workloads are pushing customers from on-premise to cloud because they lack in-house GPUs and servers, and expects more progression in that direction; no Amagi capex or capacity figures were given.
Management said GPU costs are significant for video AI but did not quantify them; token cost is a small part of AI cost in video.
demand_pricing: Management says most customers are pursuing expansion (more channels, revenue opportunities) rather than AI cost savings today, citing Jevons' paradox.
Outcome-based pricing (per transaction, per result, per success) is being discussed in some markets, but management says it is not yet visible in media.

Management says token cost is a small part of AI cost in video; GPU costs are significant. It also cited an example of a scheduler's work falling from 8 hours to about 10 minutes of review under an agentic system.
Management described the metadata and preparation workload as a headcount constraint, with media companies creating about 6 hours of unique news daily and running content across 40-plus countries.

qa_highlights.question: Can AI move production and pre-production workflows to the cloud?

544709|2026-06.headline: Gaudium IVF Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9.1% YoY to ₹19.4 crore, while reported EBITDA margin fell to 12.5% from 29% on expansion and marketing costs.
544709|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 9.1% YoY to ₹19.4 crore against ₹17.8 crore in Q1 FY26, with management attributing the slow growth to seasonality and pre-launch work. Management reiterated FY27 targets of about 30% revenue growth and 10 new hubs, but the quarter's growth rate is far below that target.

544717|2026-03.headline: CleanMax FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 28% to INR1,295 crore and PAT to INR86 crore; contracted capacity 5.7 GW with at least 1.5 GW addition guided for FY27.

Management guided to at least 1,500 MW of RE power sales additions in FY27 but gave no financial guidance. Key new risks raised were Rajasthan CTU curtailment (Bikaner 2 substation at about 30%) and the proposed deviation settlement mechanism (DSM) rules, which management has not yet quantified.

A 530 MW CTU project at Koppal in Karnataka (450 MW wind, 80 MW solar) is being added in FY27; a 525 MW CTU project in Rajasthan is about 13% of run-rate EBITDA.

demand_pricing: Data and AI customers are 42% of contracted capacity (about 2,400 MW), up from 14% (about 260 MW) on 1 April 2024; named clients include Princeton Digital Group, Iron Mountain, STT Data, and global big tech (Apple, Meta, Google, Amazon per management).

Contracted tariff on 2.6 GW under execution averages about INR3.85/unit (about 70% solar, 30% wind, negligible storage).

qa_highlights.question: Impact of Iran war and supply constraints on capex, module costs and interest rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not seen material adverse movement in equipment availability or capital costs attributable to the Iran war, while acknowledging a volatile situation.

qa_highlights.question: Share of under-construction CTU capacity, curtailment exposure and PPA protection?
qa_highlights.answer: The 530 MW Koppal CTU project is mostly wind in South India where curtailment is seen as minimal; PPAs give no protection if the grid curtails, since corporate customers do not pay for performance.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the new deviation settlement mechanism (DSM) on revenues?
qa_highlights.answer: No final decision and no internal impact estimate yet; the rules are sub-judice and the government is in talks. Storage is being evaluated to limit DSM downside, with an update in three to four months.

qa_highlights.question: Nature of INR414 crore pre-tax cash flow hedge gain and negative minority interest?
qa_highlights.answer: Hedge is a balance-sheet fair-value entry on VPPA/I-REC contracts with zero P&L impact given fixed tariffs; minority interest is negative because young SPVs (asset age under two years) carry interest and depreciation before profits.

qa_highlights.question: BESS in the contracted portfolio and tariffs?

qa_highlights.question: Impact of rising module prices on IRRs?

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA margin lower than utility peers?

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost outlook and Bikaner curtailment timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Refinancing may lower costs, but management would not make bold bets given macro risk. Bikaner 2 substation curtailment is about 30%; grid expects end by September 2026 but management urged more conservatism.

qa_highlights.question: FY27 pipeline mix and data-centre share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no reason for the wind/solar mix or the Data and AI share (42% at both start and end of FY26) to change, and says FY27 additions are already fully contracted.

qa_highlights.question: Is run-rate EBITDA adjusted for curtailment, and EBITDA per MW?

risks_watch: Rajasthan CTU curtailment: Bikaner 2 at about 30%; management sized impact at about 2.5% of run-rate EBITDA for six months at 40% backdown and about 6.5% for a full year at 50%.
DSM rules: impact not yet quantified; rules are sub-judice, and forecasting improvements are needed industry-wide.
Module cost step-up from ALMM rules from June 2026 and possible timing slippage; solar contracting paused pending government decision.
Rising interest rate environment could offset refinancing benefits; 40% of debt is fixed rate.
Ramp-up of new assets: revenue stabilisation takes three to six months after COD, and the asset-level net debt build-up depends on this.

544853|2026-06.headline: Juniper Green Q1 FY27 revenue rose 79% YoY to INR 324 crore and EBITDA 86% to INR 294 crore, with 601 MWp commissioned in the quarter.
544853|2026-06.overview: First results call as a listed company: total income INR 324 crore (+79% YoY), EBITDA INR 294 crore (+86%) at a 91% margin, and PAT INR 33 crore (+54%). Fleet CUF rose to 30.2% from 28.2% and generation grew 72% to 944 million units. Management reported record commissioning of 601 MWp in the quarter and won new SECI FDRE/thermal-mimic and GUVNL wind tenders after quarter end. Net debt-to-equity was 3.24x before IPO proceeds of INR 1,800 crore; net worth is now stated at INR 5,200 crore.

segments.name: BESS
segments.commentary: Target ~4.5 GWh installed by June 2027 and ~10 GWh by March 2028; ~4 GWh additional orders placed with Envision. Round-trip efficiency ~91%, state of health ~99.6%.

Bikaner 50 MW merchant plant curtailment ~2-2.5%; 100 MWh battery doubling to 200 MWh expected within a month.

qa_highlights.question: Does transmission delay pose a risk to the ~2 GW FY27 addition plan, and how is the TGNA route viewed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said >760 MW is already commissioned and the next ~300 MW is on STU with no grid issue. The remaining ~1 GW sits on operational substations; one ~300 MW substation should complete by December 2026. If CTU delays occur, batteries would be commissioned first and run merchant until GNA arrives.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and how much more spend is implied beyond 2,000 MW?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex was ~INR 16,000 crore as of 30 June 2026, rising to ~INR 22,000 crore by March 2027, covering ~3,900 MW commissioned by then plus CWIP for later capacity.

qa_highlights.question: How much curtailment hit Q1 and how is it being addressed?
qa_highlights.answer: Curtailment is ~2-2.5%, largely on the 50 MW Bikaner merchant plant on TGNA. Its 100 MWh battery is being doubled to 200 MWh within about a month; FDRE TGNA capacity has 400 MWh of battery, with more by October.

qa_highlights.question: What run-rate EBITDA applies to capacity added at March 2026 versus June 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Current 2,575 MW commissioned carries run-rate EBITDA of INR 1,620 crore; March 2026 capacity contributes INR 1,050 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the LOA-to-PPA conversion outlook given ~5 GW of LOAs against ~6 GW of PPAs?
qa_highlights.answer: Signed a 50 MW SJVN FDRE PPA; 550 MW of FDRE is unsigned, with 350 MW in advanced discussion with buyers confirmed and a 150 MW hybrid in very advanced talks. Management expects over 2 GW peak plus ~4 GWh BESS to be signed in the next few months, including the thermal-mimic tender.

qa_highlights.question: Where is BESS sourced, at what prices, and why is solar-plus-battery favoured over wind?
qa_highlights.answer: All ~4.5 GWh is contracted from Envision (AESC cells, PCS, EMS via Universe). Container prices were ~USD 59-60/kWh for ~2-3 GWh bought in January 2026, ~USD 65-68 now, and all-in ~USD 100-110/kWh. At ~USD 100-108/kWh, solar-plus-battery matches wind returns, so wind was cut to near-zero in newer projects.

qa_highlights.question: When can the SECI thermal-mimic project reach COD, and what are its module and transmission-charge assumptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Grid connectivity is already available in Rajasthan; COD follows PPA signing, with ~4,500 MW surplus connectivity. Module cost is INR 12.1-12.2/Wp non-DCR, with DCR modules assumed at ~INR 17/Wp; the ~75% CUF design is said to remove the transmission-charge waiver issue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PAT one-off and why was depreciation policy changed?
qa_highlights.answer: A ~INR 18 crore one-time refinancing cost hit PAT. Depreciation policy was aligned to market practice based on an external assessment; no quantified impact was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the size and economics of merchant BESS, and what margins apply?
qa_highlights.answer: ~1.5 GWh not yet linked to projects will run merchant for 1-2 years; ~700 MWh more is due by December 2026. Charging costs ~INR 1-1.50/unit versus INR 2.50 earlier; some power sold on HPDAM at up to INR 20/unit. Standalone BESS is not pursued as returns are low; new tenders target higher-teens overall returns.

risks_watch: Transmission readiness: ~1 GW of CTU capacity and a ~300 MW substation due by December 2026 must land for the 2 GW FY27 target; 250-300 MW planned in Q2 FY27.
Conversion of LOAs to PPAs: ~550 MW FDRE and the 870 MW SECI thermal-mimic tender remain unsigned; COD depends on PPA signing.
BESS cost and supply: container prices rose from ~USD 59-60 to ~USD 65-68/kWh on lithium carbonate; all 4.5 GWh is from one vendor (Envision).
Merchant exposure: ~1.5 GWh of BESS will run merchant for 1-2 years, so earnings depend on daytime charging spreads and HPDAM prices.
Thermal-mimic operations: surplus of ~1-2% expected, no revenue assumed; also the 100 MWh to 200 MWh Bikaner battery upgrade must finish in about a month.
Capex rise from ~INR 16,000 crore to ~INR 22,000 crore by March 2027, with net debt of INR 11,217 crore and debt-to-equity of 3.24x pre-IPO.
key_quotes: We have delivered our highest ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA and the highest ever renewable capacity that we have commissioned in a single quarter.
What we have done is we are getting the PC S, the EMS, and the battery container from a single entity who provides this as a fully integrated single solution.
Now given the fact that solar plus battery is then easier to execute while not losing out on the returns, it makes common sense logic.
544853|2026-06.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on execution, record commissioning and new tender wins, with the BESS and thermal-mimic economics explained in detail. Management was more cautious and vague on transmission timing, on the exact LOA-to-PPA conversion timing, and on the revenue split from BESS, which it said it could not separate from the renewable tariff.

544860|2026-06.headline: Ardee Q1 FY27 revenue rose 35.2% YoY to Rs 338.8 crore, but EBITDA was flat at Rs 33.8 crore and margin fell to 10%.
544860|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 35.2% YoY to Rs 338.8 crore on 17,645 MT sales volume, with PAT up 6% YoY to Rs 19.9 crore. EBITDA was flat at Rs 33.8 crore, with margin at 10% versus about 13% in FY26, attributed to higher domestic raw material and petroleum input costs and freight/supply-chain disruption linked to geopolitical issues. Installed capacity rose 50.9% to 156,950 MTPA effective 29 May 2026 via a brownfield debottlenecking of the existing refining unit (about Rs 15 crore capex). Management guided FY27 top-line growth of 10-20%, volume-driven, and EBITDA margin around 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volumes fall sequentially, and what is the revenue potential of the new capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited war-related import disruption and deliberately measured procurement. The new capacity is the same facility's debottlenecking, with optimum utilisation at 70-75%; the company is currently at about 65%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 10-20% top-line guidance conservative and what about FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is being conservative given trade and import/export uncertainty and would be happy to outperform; no FY28 numbers were given.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q1 inventory build temporary and what is the cash impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was temporary and driven by OEM delivery timing at quarter-end; it varies quarter to quarter by customer need, and no cash impact figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Rs 220 crore IPO working-capital allocation be used and what cash conversion cycle is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Mostly for scrap buying from new sources and export credit to new customers. Working capital days are about 95 (110 earlier), expected to stay at 90-100 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt and what is the post-IPO position?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term debt about Rs 20 crore taken on 14 August, working capital limit utilisation almost nil, and about Rs 150 crore in FDRs.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided for around 10% given geopolitical uncertainty, rather than the FY26 level of about 13%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross profit and EBITDA per ton fall versus Q4 and Q1 FY26?

risks_watch: Geopolitical disruption to Middle East shipping routes and import-based scrap procurement; management says it is not yet clear how the situation will pan out, and import share could fall if it does not improve.
Domestic scrap sourcing faces availability, pricing and GST issues from unorganised sources, and management says domestic prices are higher than imports.

Customer concentration: largest customer fell from about 70% to about 40% of revenue, but top four to five clients still account for most business.

Working capital: about 95 days now (110 earlier), guided at 90-100 days; FY27 gross working capital need above Rs 400 crore, with about Rs 220 crore from IPO proceeds. Watch cash conversion and the Q1 inventory build.
key_quotes: Right now, the overall market scenario with the whole war and being into import and export, so it is better to be conservative this year rather than say a number.

Basically, sceing the whole geopolitical scenario, which s not almost sceming to get over anytime soon, it would be better to for us to kind of say that 10% or 10% range would still be better for us to guide.

544862|2026-06.headline: Solex Q1 FY27 revenue rose 1.8% YoY to INR265.6 crore while PAT fell to INR8.3 crore (3.1% margin) on higher depreciation and finance costs.
544862|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR265.6 crore, up 1.8% YoY from INR261 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR33.8 crore (12.7% margin vs 16.4%). Depreciation rose to INR10.2 crore and finance cost to INR12.5 crore, taking PAT to INR8.3 crore (3.1% margin). Management also flagged progress on a 2.2 GW cell line, with funding and land still pending.

Sharon AI GPU capacity (8,200 B300 GPUs, Sydney SYD1 data centre) expected to go live by early November 2026 per the Kunal Bajaj reply, with billing from Q1 FY28 per another reply.
Own GPU target of about 1,500 GPUs to be deployed by January-February 2027 (mid-to-end Q4 FY27).

qa_highlights.question: Are there capex subsidies (PLI) or any client concentration risk?

544901|2026-06.headline: Purple Style Labs Q1 FY27 revenue rose to INR119 crores (from INR106 crores), but EBITDA was negative INR11 crores vs negative INR4 crores a year earlier.
544901|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was the first full quarter with the four large-format experience centres opened in FY26 (Fort Mumbai, South Ex Delhi, Linking Road Bandra, Madison Avenue New York). GMV rose to INR193 crores from INR133 crores and AOV rose to INR86,000 from INR66,000. Revenue from operations was INR119 crores, gross margin held at 36%, and EBITDA and PAT losses were wider than a year earlier on the higher fixed cost base of the new stores. Inventory and net working capital fell year on year, but borrowings rose to INR436 crores at June 2026 from INR371 crores at FY26 end.

segments.name: Mumbai (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR50 crores from INR28 crores in the first three months of FY26. Mumbai was the largest market in FY26 GMV at INR205 crores.

segments.name: Delhi (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR39 crores from INR29 crores. Delhi FY26 GMV was INR166 crores.

segments.name: Hyderabad (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR16 crores from INR10 crores.

segments.name: USA (3M FY27)
segments.commentary: Contribution rose to INR29 crores from INR20 crores. New York flagship opened in March 2026 and is the first US store; US was online-only before that.

guidance_outlook: No objective margin or profitability guidance given; management said it would refrain from it.
Q1 is the leanest quarter; management said the cost structure set in Q1 will carry into Q2 absent changes, and clearer trends are expected over the next two quarters.
No significant new experience centre expansion is planned near term; the first full year of the FY26 store investments is to be observed.

EBITDA break-even framing: on a P&L basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed for zero EBITDA, with lease-related costs of INR45 crores (lease interest plus ROU depreciation) included. On a cash basis, lease payments of INR29 crores imply a smaller gap.
Lease interest and ROU depreciation are expected to stay broadly flat unless stores change. Other finance cost should decline as operating profit reduces debt.
capex_capacity: Four large-format experience centres opened in FY26: Fort Mumbai and South Ex Delhi (operational since Q2 FY26), Linking Road Bandra (end-March 2026), and Madison Avenue New York (March 2026).
Store footprint is organised by geography, not by store, so same-store sales are not tracked. Mumbai now runs two large-format centres.
The New York lease is a June-end lease with a shorter tenure, so rent can be adjusted after 12-18 months of performance.
Inventory is expected to stay roughly flat at the current level absent further expansion. Management said inventory is around INR160 crores, with breadth-led singular-unit stock.
demand_pricing: AOV rose to INR86,000 in Q1 FY27, from INR76,000 in FY26 and INR46,000 in FY24. Store AOV is about 2.5x online AOV (India online about INR38,000 vs store about INR90,000 in FY26).
Active designer brands fell to 1,109 in FY26 from 1,910 in FY24. Top 100 designers were 67% of sales in FY24.
Average GMV per customer rose to INR108,000 in FY26 from INR67,000 in FY24. Top 50,000 customers contributed INR702 crores of FY26 GMV of INR722 crores.
Women's wear above INR1 lakh grew to INR312 crores GMV in FY26 from INR187 crores in FY24. Women's wear below INR35,000 fell to INR86 crores from INR162 crores.
Gross margin percentage is said to be broadly flat across price points. Management argued that absolute gross profit per piece rises with higher ticket size.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow still negative and borrowings rising despite lower inventory and working capital? When does the business become self-funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the lower inventory reflects better inventory management after the FY22-25 build-up, and higher customer advances (INR49 crores) helped working capital. Debt is funding interest costs, and Q1 is not operationally profitable. It asked investors to observe the next few quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Does the higher-ticket strategy improve gross margin or only AOV?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said percentage gross margin is similar across categories. The benefit is in absolute gross profit per piece (e.g., at 40% margin a INR2 lakh piece yields INR80,000 vs INR8,000 for a INR20,000 piece), plus lower supply and customer complexity from the long tail.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of outright purchase, consignment and backorder inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consignment split is business-sensitive and not disclosed. Outright purchase forms the inventory on the books. Backorder advances are about one month of revenue, and average delivery is 45-60 days, so backorder customer advances are not inventory.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for finance costs in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Lease interest plus ROU depreciation (INR45 crores in the P&L) should stay at Q1 levels absent new store changes. Other finance cost should fall as operating profit reduces debt.

qa_highlights.question: What GMV scale, gross margin and operating leverage are needed for EBITDA positivity?
qa_highlights.answer: On an EBITDA basis, gross profit of about INR55 crores would be needed. Adding the lease costs of INR45 crores (P&L) or INR29 crores (cash) raises the required gross profit. Management referred to the detailed P&L on slide 20.

qa_highlights.question: What is the New York store's AOV and break-even, and what is the SSG for mature stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated a New York store AOV of about INR1.25 lakh (about USD1,500), based on a 2.5x multiple to online AOV. It did not give a break-even GMV. Same-store growth is not tracked because the company reports by geography.

544903|2026-09.headline: Deepa Jewellers Q2 FY27 revenue rose 25% YoY to INR 626 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.24% on plain-gold mix and PAT rose 37% to INR 37 crore.
544903|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations grew 25% YoY to INR 626 crore, with EBITDA of INR 45 crore (up 17% YoY, margin 7.24%) and PAT of INR 37 crore (up 37%, margin 5.96%). H1 FY27 revenue rose 30% to INR 1,057 crore, EBITDA rose 24% to INR 84 crore (7.95% margin) and PAT rose 32% to INR 64 crore. Management attributed the Q2 growth moderation to festive demand shifting into H2, and said lower gross margin came from a plain-gold-heavy sales mix, with PAT supported by other income and a lower tax rate. The company also commenced its in-house Hyderabad manufacturing facility in September 2026 and guided to 40-45% revenue CAGR for FY27-FY29.

segments.name: Job work
segments.commentary: Volume of 318 kg in Q2 (+44% YoY) and 544 kg in H1 (+51% YoY). Realisation per gram fell to about INR 178-180 from about INR 200 a year earlier, which management attributed to plain-gold mix rather than pricing changes.

segments.name: Jewellery manufacturing (invoice/own gold)
segments.commentary: Volume of 491 kg in Q2 (broadly stable) and 783 kg in H1 (-5% YoY). Own-processing realisation fell to about INR 12,600/g from INR 14,500/g, attributed to lower gold prices, plain-gold mix and higher 18-karat sales.

segments.name: Studded vs plain gold mix
segments.commentary: Studded share was 57% of H1 FY27 sales, against 65% in FY26, with plain gold at 43%. Management targets studded share of 75% over the next three to four quarters.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR of 40-45% guided for FY27, FY28 and FY29, with FY27 growth of 40-45% compared with FY26 (March 2026) base; the 40-45% figure was also described as a 40-50% revenue CAGR for two years at a constant 24-karat gold rate of INR 50,000.
EBITDA margin expected to expand 80-120 bps over the next 4-6 quarters, driven by the Hyderabad facility, Tier-2/3 expansion, studded mix and standalone store sales.
Gross margin pressure from plain-gold mix expected to normalise in upcoming quarters.
Hedging to rise from 94% toward close to 100% of gold holdings over the next two to three quarters.
Working capital cycle (inventory days plus receivable days) expected in the 55-65 day range; inventory and receivables expected to normalise from Q3.
Internal accruals, IPO proceeds and existing debt expected to fund growth through FY29.
Effective tax rate guided at the standard 25.168%; Q2 benefit came from deferred tax on IPO expenses, with the tax shield reversing in later years.
capex_capacity: In-house manufacturing facility in Hyderabad, about 6,700 sq ft, commenced operations in September 2026.
Facility capacity of about 1.5 tonnes a year on single shift and about 2.5 tonnes a year on double shift.
Facility processed 65 kg (13% of volume) in Q1 FY27 and 167 kg (21%) in Q2 FY27; management expects about 40% in Q3 and about 50% in Q4.
Second sales office in Chennai planned for December 2026; Bangalore office planned for April-May 2027, following Vijayawada office.
Long-run target mix of 65% in-house and 35% outsourced manufacturing; outsourced work to shift in-house from Q4 FY27.
demand_pricing: Revenue concentrated in South India (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala); client base about 373 customers including 47 jewellery retail chains such as Joyalukkas, Kalyan, Lalitha and Bhima.
Q2 growth moderated as festive demand shifted into H2; H1 typically contributes about 40% of annual revenue.
Retail customers shifting from cash purchases to old-gold exchange after a gold price spike, moving sales from invoice basis to job work; management said total volume shifted rather than fell.

Job work conversion margin is about 75% and invoice-basis about 8%, with a similar ROCE/ROE in both models; job work is priced at about 1% lower wastage (4% vs 5%) because it needs no working capital.
Gold price assumption for guidance: constant 24-karat rate of INR 50,000 per 10 g; average selling gold price rose from about INR 8,000/g in FY25 to INR 11,950/g in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin and grammage realisation decline in Q2, and why did job work realisation drop about 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the change was a shift toward plain gold jewellery (lower margin than studded), not a strategic or operational change, and expects normalisation. Job work realisation fell to about INR 178 from INR 202 a year earlier (about 11%), attributed to the same SKU mix.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory and receivable days rise versus March 2026?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said March is not a like-for-like base because year-end corporate purchases stop; higher inventory came from stock built for the new Vijayawada sales office in September after IPO proceeds. Management expects normalisation from Q3 and a combined inventory plus receivable cycle of 55-65 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue outlook for the next 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth to come from new geographies (Vijayawada, Chennai, Bangalore offices), SKU expansion into studded casting, Nakshi and Tapa jewellery (16 SKUs launched in Q1), and client store expansion including franchise models. Guidance is 40-45% CAGR for FY27-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin impact of the new facility, and what EBITDA margin should be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation and karigar costs weighed on Q1 and Q2 margins; benefit expected from Q3 as more volume shifts in-house. Management guided to an 80-120 bps EBITDA margin expansion over 4-6 quarters, with a note that studded mix and standalone store sales also contribute.

qa_highlights.question: How is gold price exposure hedged, and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: 94% of gold holdings were hedged as of 30 September through gold metal loans (3.25% p.a.), MCX short futures and back-to-back unfixed purchases from bullion suppliers. Target is close to 100% within two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the effective tax rate fall to about 15%, and will it normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the standard rate is 25.168%; the lower Q2 rate reflects deferred tax on IPO expenses, which Companies Act treats against securities premium while Income Tax allows over five years. The effect is expected to even out in later years.

qa_highlights.question: Will promoters draw salary, and how will they be compensated?
qa_highlights.answer: Both Ashish Agarwal and Dev Agarwal will not draw salary from 1 October 2026, and Dev Agarwal said no salary is planned for at least 10 quarters, after which the board will decide.

risks_watch: Gross margin and realisation pressure from plain-gold mix and lower gold prices; management quantified a 50% gold price fall at about 60 bps gross margin impact.
Working capital intensity: inventory and receivable days rose versus September FY26, and growth of 40-45% needs funding from accruals, IPO proceeds and debt.
Execution risk on new Hyderabad plant ramp-up (targeted about 40% of volume in Q3 and 50% in Q4) and on Chennai and Bangalore office launches.
Shift of retail customers toward old-gold exchange could keep invoice-basis sales subdued and raise job work share.
Customer concentration in South India and in a few large jewellery chains.
Tax rate normalisation from Q2 deferred benefit back to 25.168%.
Hedging coverage to rise to close to 100%; monitor in next quarter.

Management was more evasive on specifics, notably the EBITDA margin direction (a live misstatement of 80-120 bps versus a dip was clarified on the call) and on the basis for the 40-45% CAGR. 544911|2026-06.headline: Kanohar Q1 FY27 revenue rose 103.5% YoY to INR137.1 crore, with EBITDA margin of 28.3% and order book of about INR2,026 crore.
544911|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR137.1 crore, up 103.5% YoY, with transformers at 84.9% and EPC at 14.81% of revenue. EBITDA rose 152.2% to INR38.8 crore (28.3% margin, up 550 bps) and PAT rose 140% to INR27.3 crore (19.9% margin). Consolidated order book stood at about INR2,026 crore on June 30, 2026, up 11% from March 31, 2026, after incremental orders of INR332.2 crore in Q1 and INR867.3 crore in Q2 to date. Management guided FY27 revenue of about INR950 crore with EBITDA margin similar to FY26, with H2 as the main execution period.

financial_highlights.value: Q1: INR332.2 crore; Q2 to date: INR867.3 crore

segments.name: Power Transformers / 400 kV
segments.commentary: 400 kV transformers contributed 70.16% of Q1 revenue (52% in FY26, 10.3% in FY24). Management said 400 kV, Scott-connected and shunt reactor products carry similar gross margins; about 70% of order book is power transformers, mostly 400 kV.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: EPC contributed 14.81% of Q1 revenue. Management does not disclose EBITDA separately; directionally lower than transformer margins.

segments.name: By end-user
segments.commentary: Power Transmission 85.18%, Railways 11.53%, Renewable Energy 2.84%, Power Distribution 0.23% of Q1 revenue. Shunt reactors were about 13.1% of order book at June 30.

segments.name: Voltage mix (other)
segments.commentary: 132 kV to below 220 kV at 11.38%, 220 kV to below 400 kV at 3.19%, below 132 kV at 0.23% of Q1 revenue.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of about INR950 crore, with EBITDA margin broadly similar to FY26.
FY28 revenue growth expected to be similar to FY27 guidance (about 40-45% per analyst's read, not confirmed by management).
Brownfield expansion of about 18,000 MVA at Gangol, targeted to be in place by end-FY28 / FY29; existing capacity seen sufficient through FY28.
Net working capital guided at 110-120 days.
Order book at end-FY27 may be adequate to cover FY28 and FY29 revenue, per management; no specific FY27 closing order book number given.
Shunt reactors expected to be about 10-15% of revenue on average over time.
capex_capacity: Existing capacity about 19,200 MVA across Rithani and Gangol (Meerut); Gangol about 18,000 MVA.
Q1 FY27 executed about 1,725 MVA, implying roughly 36-46% utilisation depending on base used.
Planned brownfield expansion of about 18,000 MVA at Gangol; part funded from IPO proceeds.

About 2,500 kW solar plant planned, partly funded from IPO proceeds; savings not quantified.
demand_pricing: Management estimates India 400 kV transformer market at about 60,000-70,000 MVA last year, growing 10-15% industry-wide; analyst's INR4,000-6,000 crore 400 kV market size was confirmed as 'in that range'.

Industry lead times are 18-24 months; tenders being bid are mainly for FY29-FY30 execution.
Revenue per MVA about INR6.1 lakh last year; may have risen slightly due to raw material costs.
Management said there were no new entrants in the last 3-6 months that it is aware of, but expects new entrants over time.

qa_highlights.question: How were transformer margins protected in Q1 given input cost increases and fixed-price contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most contracts carry price variation linked to the IEEMA clause, which passes through raw material moves in both directions.

qa_highlights.question: Will GEC-III drive a multi-year order tailwind for 400 kV and 500 MVA transformers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called it a multi-decadal structural tailwind; intra-state transmission is mostly 400 kV, but no split of GEC-III capacity by voltage was given.

qa_highlights.question: Can order book reach INR3,000 crore by FY27 end, and 40-45% YoY growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to confirm; said Q2 execution will reduce the order book slightly, and end-FY27 book may cover FY28-FY29 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 1H-weak, 2H-heavy revenue pattern a continuing trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, management said H1 is typically softer and H2 heavier, an industry trend.

qa_highlights.question: Will new 400 kV capacity pressure margins beyond 3-4 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects visibility for 3-4 years from current order book and tenders; beyond that, short-term supply-demand mismatch and margin pressure are possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why was FY24 a revenue decline and why is utilisation low; are exports planned?

544913|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 36% YoY to Rs.107 crore and EBITDA rose 9% to Rs.23 crore, with margin at 21.3% and a Rs.982 crore order book.

PAT of Rs.17 crore grew more slowly than EBITDA due to lower other income (prior-year property sale gain) and higher depreciation from new capacity. qa_highlights.question: What is the pipeline now versus last quarter, and when will conversion and growth show up?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pipeline is about USD 28 million versus USD 25 million last quarter, with better quality. Next quarter looks muted, with growth hoped for in H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue guidance still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated INR 1,200-1,250 crore, about 25% growth on INR 1,007 crore in FY26, and will restate at end of Q2 if needed.

qa_highlights.question: Which verticals drive growth in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Emerging verticals first, then BFSI and logistics. Digital commerce has the most headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: Why is employee cost falling and what will new senior hires add?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount falls from AI productivity, AI agents in support functions, and a shift to outcome-based deals. Two senior hires were funded by repurposing costs of founders who exited after earnouts, so management does not expect employee cost to rise.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company letting go of tail clients, and how is client concentration changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it is exiting accounts without scale potential. Top 10 concentration fell from 58% to 56%, and it has no target to reduce it further.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue comes from AI and what is the AI deal-size trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not break out AI revenue. It said every project includes AI, and pure AI work is limited to AI co-innovation labs.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue comes from the US and how will it change?
qa_highlights.answer: US share is 52% (management corrected from 55%), with a target of at least 65% in two to three years.

risks_watch: Q2 FY27 is expected to be muted, and FY27 guidance of INR 1,200-1,250 crore requires a sharp H2 recovery from a flat H1.
Deal conversion is slow as the shift to larger outcome-based deals lengthens decision cycles.
Digital commerce faces the most headwinds, and BFSI revenue is flat QoQ.
Management did not quantify the number of accounts exited; it promised to send figures later. Pipeline figure of USD 28 million is also to be confirmed in writing.
Long-term INR 500 million target (FY30) was raised by an analyst but not addressed by management.
Competition from larger IT players moving down into smaller deals.
Appraisals next quarter could push up employee costs.
590051|2026-06.management_tone: Cautious on near-term demand and conversion, with management openly saying Q2 will be muted and that they do not expect improvement soon. It is more confident on the medium-term pipeline, AI productivity and the move to managed services, but it gave few hard numbers beyond the FY27 guidance it reiterated.
key_quotes: Decision making is getting delayed unfortunately, and we are pushing as hard as we can, but there is a limit to how much you can fight the industry
Numbers will come, growth will come, it won't happen overnight.
Nothing is normalizing.
Nothing is pilot, everything is in production.
